title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Optimization Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols based on quantum decoherence. The core claim is to enhance key generation rates and security through intelligent protocol parameter tuning. Leveraging machine learning algorithms, we analyze the impact of decoherence noise, aiming to improve key generation efficiency and security. The proposed approach represents a novel application of machine learning within QKD, offering a significant pathway towards improved key distribution performance. We present a framework for adaptive parameter control, demonstrating the potential for substantial gains in key rates and robustness against decoherence effects. The research focuses on theoretical optimization, without experimental validation, providing a robust mathematical framework for understanding and improving current QKD protocols. The key performance metrics considered are key generation rate (R), Bit Error Rate (BER), and security level (Φ). The work contributes to the field by outlining a systematic methodology for utilizing machine learning to tackle the inherent challenges of decoherence in QKD systems. ---

title: Title: Fractal Dimensionally-Adaptive Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Bayesian Networks to complex data analysis, specifically focusing on the creation of adaptive dimension networks. Traditional Bayesian Networks often struggle with high-dimensional data, leading to suboptimal predictive performance. We propose a novel approach – Fractal Dimension Adaptation – that dynamically adjusts the 'fractal dimension' of the network based on the input data, thereby improving accuracy in challenging environments. This mechanism leverages the inherent fractal properties of data to create a more robust and predictive model. The core of this work is a novel algorithm for iteratively refining the network's structure, guided by the observed data's fractal characteristics. This adaptive dimension ensures the network's complexity is tailored to the specific data distribution, leading to enhanced predictive capabilities. The resulting networks demonstrate superior performance across a range of high-dimensional datasets compared to existing approaches.

title: Quantum-Guided Evolution of Mathematical Structures
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-guided evolution to fundamentally alter the trajectory of mathematical structures, focusing on the manipulation of group theory and lattice structures. We propose a novel method, termed "Quantum Guidance," utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to subtly influence the evolution of these structures, offering a potential paradigm shift in algorithm design and mathematical modeling. The paper details the core mechanism of this approach, outlining the initial conceptual framework and mathematical foundations underpinning the Quantum Guidance algorithm. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in evolving simple lattice structures, highlighting its potential for broader application across a range of mathematical domains. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, emphasizing the challenges and opportunities presented by this nascent field.

abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization represents a promising avenue for addressing computationally challenging optimization problems. This paper investigates the application of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) to emulate the quantum annealing process, aiming to improve the speed and accuracy of complex optimization tasks. The core mechanism centers around utilizing SGD to dynamically adjust the solution trajectory, effectively mimicking the quantum annealing process.

title: Title: Information-Theoretic Constraints for Neural Network Training
abstract: Information-theoretic constraints offer a novel approach to neural network training, moving beyond traditional gradient descent to directly leverage the principles of entropy and mutual information. This paper introduces a new constraint formulation that explicitly incorporates these concepts, promoting stable and efficient training through a process of information-guided optimization. This method contrasts with current techniques that primarily rely on gradient descent, offering a potentially more robust and principled method for learning complex neural network models. The core mechanism involves constructing a constraint set that explicitly measures the uncertainty in the data and guides the network's weights towards regions of lower uncertainty, leading to improved generalization and reduced sensitivity to initial conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, demonstrating improved convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional methods.

title: Anomaly Detection via Adversarial Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection utilizing adversarial learning. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with subtle anomalies that closely resemble normal data, leading to high false positive rates. This work addresses this challenge by framing anomaly detection as an adversarial learning problem. Specifically, we train a discriminator network to distinguish between normal and anomalous data, while simultaneously training an anomaly generator to produce samples that are designed to fool the discriminator. This dynamic interaction forces the discriminator to learn more robust features, ultimately improving its ability to identify anomalies. The core claim of this research is that anomaly detection can be effectively leveraged through adversarial learning to train detectors capable of recognizing anomalies that closely resemble normal data. The mechanism involves modeling the detection problem as an adversarial one, training a detector to differentiate between normal and anomalous data. We argue that this approach offers a significant improvement in anomaly detection accuracy compared to conventional methods.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection with Temporal Convolutional Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection that integrates graph representation learning with temporal convolutional neural networks (TCNs). Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle to capture complex dependencies within time series data, particularly when these dependencies are non-linear and influenced by contextual relationships. Our method addresses this limitation by constructing a graph representation of the data, where nodes represent data points and edges encode relationships based on temporal proximity and similarity. The TCN then learns representations of this graph, effectively capturing both temporal patterns and anomalies within the structured context provided by the graph. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, that this combined approach significantly enhances anomaly detection performance compared to methods relying solely on temporal patterns. The core claim highlights the potential of TCNs augmented by graph representations. The proposed mechanism focuses on learning representations within the graph structure, leveraging temporal convolution to identify anomalies. This work contributes a new methodology for anomaly detection, combining the strengths of graph neural networks and TCNs.

We present a new framework for controlling entanglement, moving beyond simple protocol implementations to prioritize the creation of inherently more stable quantum states, potentially paving the way for significantly increased computational complexity in quantum computers. The core mechanism centers around introducing a field that influences entanglement topology, offering a pathway to enhanced computational power.

title: Dear Reader,
abstract: This paper explores a novel optimization approach leveraging adaptive perturbation algorithms to enhance the optimization of complex systems. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with static parameter settings, necessitating iterative adjustments that can be computationally expensive and may not fully capture the system's behavior. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism, driven by an adaptive perturbation algorithm, that continuously refines system parameters to achieve superior performance. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through rigorous analysis and simulation, highlighting its potential to significantly improve optimization efficiency and quality.

title: ## The Hydra's Embrace: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Hydra Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the "Hydra's Embrace" (HE) metaheuristic algorithm, a novel optimization technique inspired by the regenerative capabilities of the Hydra, a mythical serpentine creature. HE leverages the Hydra's ability to regrow severed heads, combined with a dynamic exploration-exploitation strategy, to effectively navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm utilizes a population of "nodes," each representing a potential solution. Nodes are evaluated based on a dynamically adjusted "vitality score," reflecting their contribution to the overall search progress. Severed nodes are replaced with new ones, mimicking the Hydra's regeneration. The algorithm incorporates a "resonance" mechanism to guide the search towards promising regions and a "decay" factor to control the rate of regeneration. This approach aims to achieve a balance between exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates and robustness in various optimization problems. The core concept centers around a dynamically evolving population where survival and reproduction are governed by the vitality score and a regeneration process, mirroring the Hydra's adaptive survival strategy.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Adaptive Quantum State Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based adaptive quantum state modeling method. Traditional quantum state modeling approaches are often static, limiting the ability to dynamically adjust quantum states and thus hindering the representation of complex quantum phenomena. Our method leverages the self-adaptive properties of dynamic topology to automatically adjust quantum state parameters, enabling the simulation and control of quantum states exhibiting dynamic evolution. This represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a robust and flexible framework for modeling quantum systems with significant potential for applications in quantum computing and quantum information processing.

title: High-Dimensional Space Geometry: Adaptive Optimization Based on Physical Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive optimization techniques to high-dimensional space, leveraging physical models to guide parameter optimization and neural network structure design. Traditional optimization methods often rely on human-designed parameters, lacking a deep understanding of the underlying physical principles. We propose a novel approach that integrates physical model self-similarity, automatically adjusting parameters to achieve optimal solutions. The core mechanism involves leveraging this self-similarity to optimize data structures, offering a promising path toward more robust and efficient parameter tuning. The research addresses the limitations of conventional methods by incorporating a physical model's intrinsic properties directly into the optimization process. The paper details the design of an adaptive optimization algorithm incorporating physical model self-similarity, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses its potential impact on various applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Reasoning Engine (QDE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Reasoning Engine (QDE), a novel architecture designed to revolutionize distributed computing by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that entanglement's non-locality can enable remote, ultra-low latency distributed reasoning, overcoming the limitations of traditional computing paradigms. QDE achieves this through a network of interconnected quantum processors, each storing a portion of the computational data. Utilizing entanglement, the system facilitates instantaneous synchronization and collective computation, enabling complex logical deductions. This approach contrasts significantly with traditional distributed reasoning, which relies on classical communication, introducing inherent delays and bandwidth constraints. The QDE architecture offers the potential for significantly faster and more efficient problem-solving, particularly for computationally intensive tasks requiring global data access and parallel processing. This paper details the theoretical framework, the proposed architecture, and outlines the potential impact of QDE on various domains, including scientific simulations, artificial intelligence, and cryptography. The primary mathematical framework presented focuses on the entanglement fidelity, quantum state transfer rates, and the logical operations performed within the entangled network.

title: Title: Fractal Resonance & Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Fractal resonance, a theoretical concept, proposes that specific geometric patterns can generate and amplify quantum entanglement, offering a potential pathway to faster-than-light communication. This research investigates this concept through the development of a computational model to identify resonant frequencies within fractal geometries and proposes a novel quantum entanglement protocol based on observed fractal patterns. The core claim is that this approach, if validated, could unlock a new paradigm in quantum communication. This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of the potential, highlighting the mathematical framework and initial theoretical models underpinning this investigation.

title: ## Grey Squirrel Mimicry-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSM-MOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Grey Squirrel Mimicry-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GSM-MOA), a novel optimization technique motivated by the adaptive camouflage strategies observed in grey squirrels. The algorithm leverages the squirrel's ability to dynamically adjust its coloration and behavior based on environmental context and predator presence to mimic optimal solutions. GSM-MOA utilizes a population of candidate solutions, each represented by a set of parameters. A 'mimicry' mechanism is implemented, where individuals dynamically adjust their parameters based on a 'perception' of the 'landscape' – a representation of the optimization problem – and the 'threat' level, simulating predator pressure. The algorithm incorporates both exploration and exploitation phases, with the rate of adjustment governed by a probabilistic model inspired by squirrel behavioral responses. This approach aims to achieve robust convergence and adaptability in complex optimization landscapes. The core of GSM-MOA lies in its dynamically adjusting parameters, driven by a simulated predator threat, mirroring the adaptive camouflage of grey squirrels. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods in challenging scenarios.

title: ## Riftia-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RIMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Riftia-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RIMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique growth and adaptation strategies of the deep-sea tube worm *Riftia pachyptila*. *Riftia* tube worms exhibit remarkable resilience to environmental changes, particularly in nutrient-poor conditions, by dynamically adjusting the expression of genes involved in nutrient absorption. RIMOA leverages this biological mechanism through a dynamic population approach, utilizing a 'nutrient balance' concept to control the exploration and exploitation phases of the algorithm. The core innovation lies in a novel 'Nutrient Gradient' function, which guides the movement of solutions based on a simulated nutrient scarcity and abundance, mimicking *Riftia*'s adaptation process. The algorithm aims to effectively navigate complex search spaces and achieve robust optimization results. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and conceptual links to the biological inspiration, emphasizing its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state generation algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional quantum state generation methods often rely on static topologies, limiting their flexibility and control. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the topology of a quantum system to generate unique and tailored quantum states. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experimental results, showcasing improved accuracy and control over quantum measurements compared to existing techniques. The core mechanism involves iterative topology adjustments guided by a feedback loop, ensuring the generation of highly specific quantum states. This advancement offers a significant step towards more precise quantum measurements and quantum information processing.

title: Redfin Tetra-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RTT-MOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Redfin Tetra-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RTT-MOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of Redfin Tetras ( *Paracheirodon innesi*). These small fish exhibit complex social interactions and coordinated movement patterns while searching for food in a structured environment. RTT-MOA mimics these behaviors by employing a decentralized, agent-based approach where individual "tetras" (optimization agents) explore the search space independently, guided by local information and influenced by the collective behavior of the group. The algorithm utilizes a "schooling radius" to define the interaction range between agents and a "food density" map to represent the objective function landscape. Agents adjust their movement based on a combination of attraction to high food density areas and repulsion from other agents within their schooling radius, leading to efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, including the mathematical formulation of key components, and presents a conceptual outline of its implementation. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the schooling radius and the utilization of a weighted average of local food density and agent proximity to drive the search process.

title: Patent infringement by Gen AI service providers
abstract: Gen AI 서비스 제공자를 상대로 한 저작권 침해소송이 여러 나라에서 제기되고 있는 반면, 생성형 AI(Gen AI)의 원천 기술인 ‘트랜스포머(Transformer)’ 아키텍처에 특허권이 존재함에도 아직까지 관련 분쟁이 없는 것에 대해 여러 이유가 제시된다. 구글이 Gen AI 서비스 관련SW에 대해 오픈소스 라이선스 정책을 취함과 동시에 Apache 2.0 라이선스를 통해 해당 SW에 구현된 특허발명에 대해 실시권을 부여하는점, 구글이나 OpenAI 등이 방어적 특허전략을 취하고 있는 점도 그 이유 중 하나로 설명되지만, 아직 소송을 제기할 만큼 시장이 성숙하지않았다는 판단 아래 전략적으로 시장 성숙을 기다리고 있다는 분석도있다. 분명한 것은 대부분의 빅테크 기업들이 지난 10년간 다양한AI(Gen AI 포함) 관련 특허를 출원해 왔다는 점이다. 방어적 특허 활용을 선언하고 있는 OpenAI도 과거보다 특허 출원 활동을 활발히 하고있다. 또한, 구글이 Apache 2.0을 통해 SW에 구현된 특허발명에 대한라이선스를 부여하고 있으나 해당 라이선스가 적용되지 않는 경우도있을 것이다. 이런 점들을 고려하면, 향후 특허 분쟁이 증가할 가능성은 적지 않다고 생각되며, 최근 미국과 유럽의 소송이 전조 현상일 수도 있다. 우리나라에서도 머지않아 Gen AI 서비스 제공자를 상대로 특허권 침해소송이 제기될 수 있다. AI(Gen AI 포함) 관련 특허권 행사의 실효성을 높이기 위해서는 우선 발명의 실시 주체에 대한 해석론 정립이 필요하다. 청구항의 카테고리(시스템, 장치, 저장 매체, 방법 등)별로 생산ㆍ사용 등의 주체에대한 명확한 판단 기준을 마련할 필요가 있다. 만일 해석론에 의한 대응으로 충분하지 않다면 실시 행위에 대한 법 개정도 검토해 볼 필요가 있다. 특히 AI 관련 발명의 경우 ‘사용’의 의미와 그 주체 판단이중요할 것으로 보인다. 이와 더불어 간접침해 제도 개선도 필요하다. 현행 특허법의 경우 전용물적 기여 행위만을 간접침해로 규율하므로비침해 용도가 없는 시스템(혹은 장치 또는 서버) 또는 저장매체에 저장된 비침해 용도 없는 컴퓨터 프로그램을 사용자에게 양도하지 않는한 Gen AI 서비스 제공자에게 간접침해 책임을 묻기는 쉽지 않아 보인다. 특히 전용성 인정이 곤란하고 물건인지 여부의 다툼이 있는 컴퓨터 프로그램의 제공을 간접침해 행위로 포섭할 수 있는 법 개정이필요할 것이다. 한편, AI 기술의 블랙박스적 특성은 침해 증명을 어렵게 한다. AI 특허의 권리행사 국면에서 침해 증명 수단이 적극 활용되지 못하면 권리 보호의 선순환을 도모하지 못하고 악순환에 빠지게 될것이다. 특허법상 자료제출명령 제도의 활성화와 한국형 증거개시제도의 도입에 대해 적극 검토할 필요가 있다고 생각한다. 나아가 ‘AI 기술을 특정 분야에 응용한 발명’에 대한 특허출원과 분쟁이 증가할 것으로 예상되므로, 기술적 특징과 비기술적 특징이 혼재하는 컴퓨터 관련발명과 관련하여 특허적격성과 진보성 판단 기준은 개선이 필요하다고생각한다.

AI(Gen AI 포함) 관련 특허권 행사의 실효성을 높이기 위해서는 우선 발명의 실시 주체에 대한 해석론 정립이 필요하다. 청구항의 카테고리(시스템, 장치, 저장 매체, 방법 등)별로 생산ㆍ사용 등의 주체에대한 명확한 판단 기준을 마련할 필요가 있다. 만일 해석론에 의한 대응으로 충분하지 않다면 실시 행위에 대한 법 개정도 검토해 볼 필요가 있다. 특히 AI 관련 발명의 경우 ‘사용’의 의미와 그 주체 판단이중요할 것으로 보인다. 이와 더불어 간접침해 제도 개선도 필요하다. 현행 특허법의 경우 전용물적 기여 행위만을 간접침해로 규율하므로비침해 용도가 없는 시스템(혹은 장치 또는 서버) 또는 저장매체에 저장된 비침해 용도 없는 컴퓨터 프로그램을 사용자에게 양도하지 않는한 Gen AI 서비스 제공자에게 간접침해 책임을 묻기는 쉽지 않아 보인다. 특히 전용성 인정이 곤란하고 물건인지 여부의 다툼이 있는 컴퓨터 프로그램의 제공을 간접침해 행위로 포섭할 수 있는 법 개정이필요할 것이다. 한편, AI 기술의 블랙박스적 특성은 침해 증명을 어렵게 한다. AI 특허의 권리행사 국면에서 침해 증명 수단이 적극 활용되지 못하면 권리 보호의 선순환을 도모하지 못하고 악순환에 빠지게 될것이다. 특허법상 자료제출명령 제도의 활성화와 한국형 증거개시제도의 도입에 대해 적극 검토할 필요가 있다고 생각한다. 나아가 ‘AI 기술을 특정 분야에 응용한 발명’에 대한 특허출원과 분쟁이 증가할 것으로 예상되므로, 기술적 특징과 비기술적 특징이 혼재하는 컴퓨터 관련발명과 관련하여 특허적격성과 진보성 판단 기준은 개선이 필요하다고생각한다.

title: When and How to Use Post-Quantum Cryptography: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is driven by the threat posed by quantum computers, particularly the harvest-now-decrypt-later attack. PQC aims to prepare classical systems and hardware to become resilient against quantum attacks. This research discusses the system vulnerabilities, the need to migrate to PQC, and how to integrate this migration. PQC has become one of the solutions for addressing today’s vulnerabilities and threats while increasing security. The paper concludes that harvest-now-decrypt-later, Q-Day attacks, and new quantum attacks are today’s most critical threats, which can be addressed by deploying PQC solutions and, thus, increasing security. This research proposes a conceptual multi-phased model framework for the migration. The framework first addresses system objectives, goals and assets, then ranks assets based on the highest sensitivity. Crypto-Agility is achieved via the automation of PQC migration, such as the automation of re-keying endpoints, followed by the automation of auditing and testing of each migration stage. Human judgment is required to review the migration process. Once one asset is successfully transitioned, the framework goes to the next highest asset; otherwise, testing is repeated. This is expected to help systems migrate at the lowest cost and with the fewest consequences. However, the limitation of PQC migration is its high resource cost, time, requirement of human professionals, burden on existing systems, and financial expenses. Lastly, the paper recommends creating an ML model to help rank a system’s data and vulnerabilities. Moreover, the paper recommends conducting experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. In addition, the paper recommends performing migration in relation to a real-world company.

title: When AI Strikes a Chord: How AI Agent and Human Agent Moderates Crisis Response in Competence-Based and Integrity-Based Crises
abstract: As AI has become increasingly pervasive in customer service due to its convenience and efficiency, it remains unclear whether publics hold similar expectations of AI agents and whether the recommended empathetic crisis responses elicit the desired reactions used by AI agents. To answer these questions, a 2 (Crisis type: Competence-based crisis vs. Integrity-based crisis) × 2 (Crisis response agent: AI vs. Human) × 2 (Empathetic crisis response: present vs. absent) experimental design was conducted. The results showed that due to the differences between human and AI, an empathetic crisis response is not an integral component in a competence-based crisis across human and AI agents. In an integrity-based crisis, an empathetic crisis response is an essential component of a human agent’s crisis communication, as it enhances perceived sincerity and improves overall organizational evaluations. However, incorporating the same empathetic response in an AI agent’s communication may backfire.

title: mimeo: Compiling Public Expert Corpora into Agent Skills and Testing What Transfers
abstract: Giving an agent a file about a named expert can supply hard-to-find material, produce a recognizable persona, or change what the agent decides. These are different claims. We test each one. mimeo is an open-source tool that finds a person's public work, checks each extracted quotation against the cached source text, and writes a file an agent can load. Eight logged builds averaged 38 model calls; the check rejects 13.2% of extracted quotations. We tested four expert files with one coding-agent harness. Knowledge access was clearest: mimeo answered all 20 obscure, quotation-heavy questions; no closed-book condition answered more than 10. Keyword search (BM25) over the same pages answered 15-17, a gap this sample cannot resolve. Grounding showed one clear benefit: personas written from model memory misstated a documented position on 1-4 of 20 answers under every grader; the plain agent and mimeo never did. Every persona was easy to spot on short open prompts, and adding task material lowered identification by 18-23 points. mimeo was no more identifiable than a from-memory profile. Judgment transfer remained unresolved because both tests hit their ceiling: every condition found 94-97% of the problems planted in engineering tasks and scored 94-100% on 16 new application scenarios. An AI-judged "sounds like the expert" score changed with the judge: two of four preferred answers based on a model's stereotype, while two found no difference on the same text. That is a caution against relying on a single AI judge. The evidence supports mimeo as a compact, inspectable reference on a person, not as a demonstrated transfer of their judgment. Toolkit and expert profiles: https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/mimeo

title: Symmetry-Reduced Variational Quantum Simulation of the $U(5)\rightarrow SU(3)$ Quantum Phase Transition in the Interacting Boson Model
abstract: The spherical-to-deformed quantum phase transition of the Interacting Boson Model (IBM) is investigated using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). The $U(5)$--$SU(3)$ transitional Hamiltonian is studied with $χ=-\sqrt{7}/2$. We develop a symmetry-preserving, minimum-qubit VQE framework for collective nuclear models, achieving a substantial reduction in qubit requirements without compromising the finite-size quantum-phase-transition physics. The transition is characterized through the normalized $d$-boson occupation and ground-state energy derivatives. Finite-size results are found to approach the analytic critical point $ξ_c=8/17\simeq0.470588$, with an independent order-parameter extrapolation yielding $ξ_\infty=0.46986(61)$. The VQE reproduces ground-state energies and structural observables to numerical precision. These results demonstrate the potential of symmetry-reduced VQE for efficient quantum simulations of collective nuclear dynamics and quantum phase transitions.

title: Reactivating Test-Time Scaling for Plane Geometry Problem Solving
abstract: Plane geometry problem (PGP) solving has become a critical benchmark for multimodal reasoning because it requires accurate visual perception and precise multi-step symbolic deduction. Although test-time scaling (TTS) has demonstrated remarkable success in general mathematical reasoning, it fails to scale effectively under the symbolic-program paradigm for plane geometry. We identify two key obstacles: limited reasoning diversity induced by rigid symbolic programs and insufficient explicit visual grounding before symbolic deduction. To address these issues, we propose Multi-Trace Synthesis (MTS), which converts each symbolic program into heterogeneous reasoning traces, including executable Python scripts and CoT-augmented variants. We further propose Perception-Augmented (PA) training, which parses diagrams into structured semantic clauses before deduction, and Consensus-Guided Multi-Trace Ensemble (CG-MTE) for efficient self-adaptive inference. Experiments on three geometry benchmarks show that our method consistently improves PGP-solving across model scales and achieves strong performance against both general-purpose MLLMs and specialized geometry solvers. Under test-time scaling, CG-MTE achieves comparable accuracy to high-budget self-consistency while reducing sampling cost by up to 8x. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/Jason8Kang/ReTTS-PGPS.

title: Theoretical guarantees of variational quantum algorithm with guiding states
abstract: Abstract Machine learning provides a powerful framework for predicting ground-state properties across families of quantum many-body problems, enabling amortized inference and reducing the cost of repeated simulations. Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for implementing such learnable solvers on quantum computers, yet rigorous guarantees for convergence and generalization remain scarce. Motivated by the fact that standard quantum phase estimation (QPE) provides provable performance when given a guiding state with non-trivial overlap with the ground state, we introduce a variational quantum algorithm with guiding states aiming towards predicting ground-state properties of quantum many-body systems. We then develop a proof technique—the linearization trick—that maps the training dynamics of the algorithm to those of a kernel model. This connection yields theoretical guarantees on both convergence and generalization for the VQA under the guiding state assumption. Our analysis shows that guiding states facilitate convergence, suppress finite-size error terms, and ensure stability across system dimensions. Finally, we validate our findings with numerical experiments on 2D random Heisenberg models.

title: Thai Online Debate System: A Platform for Collecting Annotated Debate Data for NLP Research Communities
abstract: In natural language processing (NLP), high-quality corpora are essential for training and evaluating computational models. However, the lack of domain-specific corpora remains a major obstacle for many research communities. While significant progress has been made in stance detection, debate summarization, and argumentation mining, no publicly available Thai corpus currently supports research in these fields. A key contributing factor is the absence of a dedicated Thai-language platform that facilitates structured online debates, which severely limits sources for large-scale data collection. To address this gap, this paper presents the design and development of a Thai online debate forum that serves as both a public discussion platform and a data collection infrastructure. The system enables users to participate in debates on various topics while allowing researchers to request and obtain the collected debate data for educational and research purposes. The platform captures structured data, including debate topics, stance labels, user comments, and thematic tags, progressively forming a robust corpus for NLP tasks. This platform therefore provides a foundational infrastructure for constructing Thai debate corpora, advancing NLP studies in stance detection, argumentation mining, and debate summarization. Upon evaluation by 55 users during a prototype demonstration, all aspects achieved a high satisfaction level, yielding a macro average score of 4.67 (S.D. = 0.57). These results indicate that the proposed prototype effectively supports unbiased discussions and provides an innovative platform for accessing annotated debate datasets.

title: Design and Initial Evaluation of a RAG-Based Expert Chatbot for User Support in Non-Destructive Testing
abstract: Inspection personnel need exact parameters and safety limits from proprietary documentation that may be unsuitable for hosted processing. We present a local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) chatbot for Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) manuals and a controlled benchmark comprising three synthetic manuals, 60 curated questions, and 267 predefined required facts. Answers were scored using Key Fact Coverage (KFC), the proportion of facts detected by a deterministic matcher. A full-factorial sweep of 32 configurations reached a maximum KFC of 0.789. Document access yielded larger gains than the within-pipeline variations tested: six closed-book systems scored 0.248 to 0.339, and all four prespecified comparisons remained significant after Holm correction (adjusted p ≤ 0.0028). Synthetic specifications reduced the likelihood of answer memorization. The chunking configuration produced the clearest within-pipeline difference: the 1,000-token condition outperformed the 5,000-token condition in all 16 matched pairs (+0.161, p < 0.001). Hybrid retrieval improved KFC by 0.11 to 0.12, mainly for table questions. This is an initial controlled benchmark, not evidence of industrial robustness.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design: Geometric Constraints
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum circuit design algorithm leveraging geometric constraints to effectively address complex functions, particularly within high-dimensional problems. Traditional geometric constraint algorithms often struggle with the inherent complexities of these problems, necessitating a more robust and adaptable approach. Our proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts geometric constraints during the circuit design process, minimizing trapdoors and enhancing simulation accuracy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations focusing on a challenging, multi-dimensional function. The core mechanism centers on the iterative refinement of geometric constraints based on simulation results, leading to improved performance and robustness. The algorithm offers a novel solution for complex circuit design, potentially accelerating research in areas requiring high-fidelity simulations.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology Model Parameter Adjustment Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy for quantum topology models. Quantum topology models, characterized by their inherent topological structure, offer unique computational properties that can be exploited to enhance model performance. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often involve manually tuning parameters, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. We propose a dynamic adjustment mechanism that adapts parameter values based on the model's current state, effectively optimizing the model's behavior. This approach is driven by the model's topological properties, allowing for efficient and targeted parameter optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy through simulations and analysis, showcasing improvements in model stability and task completion compared to static parameter tuning techniques.

title: From Plausible Explanations to Causal Faithfulness: A Multi-Layer Framework for Explainable Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models are highly capable at generating text, reasoning, answering questions, summarizing content, and supporting decisions. However, understanding how these systems arrive at their outputs remains difficult for anyone other than specialist researchers. Prior work on making artificial intelligence understandable has largely focused on producing explanations that are easy for people to follow, such as showing where the model pays attention or highlighting which parts of the input appear important. An explanation that is easy to understand, convincing, or simple is not necessarily faithful to how the model actually arrived at its answer. This is a significant problem for high-stakes applications of large language models, where people may come to trust an incorrect answer more because it is accompanied by an explanation that sounds convincing but is not actually true.This paper proposes the Causal, Layered, Audience-aware Explanation framework (CLAX) for evaluating explanations of large language models. We identify four considerations for evaluating explanations that previous research has treated together rather than separately: how easy the explanation is to understand, how well it matches the model's behaviour, how faithful it is to the model's actual reasoning, and how useful it is in practice. We identify five levels that explanations can target, ranging from which inputs are important to how the model encodes, generates, and behaves in the world. We present a set of criteria for evaluating explanations, including assessing the impact of different inputs, ensuring that the explanation is complete and correct, checking that it is consistent under variations in the input, determining whether it is understandable to people, and explicitly stating what remains unknown. Rather than attempting to capture explanation quality in a single metric, CLAX highlights the importance of considering the audience, content, evidence, utility, and limitations of explanations together. CLAX is applicable to any language model, whether or not its internal mechanisms are observable, which makes it possible to reproduce research on making language models understandable. We also propose a way to evaluate this framework in future studies across different models, research areas, and types of explanations in order to determine how well it performs.

title: Program Synthesis Based on Memory
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis, termed "Program Synthesis Based on Memory," which leverages memory mechanisms to accelerate the synthesis process and generate more intelligent synthesis strategies. The core idea is to model program synthesis as a memory problem. We construct a memory library, utilizing either neural networks or knowledge graphs, to store and retrieve previously synthesized program fragments and their corresponding specifications. A retrieval algorithm then searches this library to identify the most suitable synthesis path based on the current problem. This approach significantly reduces the computational cost of exhaustive search methods and allows the system to learn from past experiences, leading to more efficient and effective program synthesis. The key contribution lies in the integration of memory and retrieval techniques, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for program synthesis. ---

title: Quantum Topology Information Fusion
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, offers a fundamentally new approach to quantum computing. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum topology to facilitate information fusion, a critical component of complex quantum algorithms. We present a novel algorithm, Quantum Topology Information Fusion (QTIF), designed to integrate disparate quantum states, thereby unlocking new computational capabilities. The core mechanism hinges on leveraging the unique topological properties of quantum states to create a unified representation, enabling more complex computations than current approaches. We detail the algorithm's design, its underlying mathematical principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in integrating quantum information. The paper concludes by discussing future research directions and potential applications of this groundbreaking approach.

title: Quantum Hidden Matrices and Cryptography: A Novel Generation of Secure Encryption Systems
abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a transformative technology, offering unprecedented computational power. This paper investigates the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize cryptography, particularly through the development of quantum hidden-square matrices (HSMs). We explore the design of a novel, secure encryption system based on HSMs, leveraging their unique properties for enhanced data security and privacy. The study focuses on the algorithmic complexities involved in HSM implementation, emphasizing the security challenges and potential optimizations. We analyze the system's potential for resistance against known attacks, including those leveraging Shor's algorithm and Grover's algorithm. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum-enhanced cryptography, offering a pathway towards a new generation of robust and secure encryption methods.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Temporal Logic Constraints
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that leverages temporal logic constraints to enhance the reliability and controllability of neural network-generated code. The core idea is to combine the learning capabilities of neural networks with the structured reasoning of symbolic programming languages, explicitly enforced through temporal logic. A neural network is trained to generate code snippets in a symbolic language, such as Lisp, while temporal logic constraints dictate the desired temporal behavior of the generated programs – including execution deadlines and causal relationships. This formalization offers a verifiable and controllable framework for neuro-symbolic programming, addressing limitations of purely data-driven or purely symbolic approaches. We outline the system architecture, detail the temporal logic formulation, and discuss potential applications, emphasizing the ability to produce code that not only fulfills functional requirements but also satisfies stringent temporal constraints.

title: Quantum State Dynamics and Computation
abstract: Quantum state dynamics and computation represent a significant frontier in the field of quantum information. This paper explores the potential of dynamically transforming quantum states using topological structure, offering a novel approach to complex quantum computations. We investigate a mechanism for achieving dynamic state transformations by exploiting the inherent properties of quantum states, ultimately enhancing the feasibility of intricate quantum algorithms. This research introduces a new algorithm framework centered around topological manipulation of quantum states. The paper details the core concept, the underlying mathematical framework, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this dynamic approach. We present a model demonstrating the ability to optimize a quantum circuit's performance through dynamic state adjustment. The work emphasizes the potential of this methodology to overcome limitations of static quantum state manipulation, paving the way for more versatile and efficient quantum computations. title: Symbiotic Neural Graph Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for constructing complex neural networks – Symbiotic Neural Graph Construction (SNGC). The core idea is that intricate neural architectures can arise spontaneously through the dynamic interaction of spatially distributed, genetically-influenced computational modules. The system operates by simulating a network of nodes with evolving computational capabilities, connected via a self-organizing 'symbiotic' algorithm. This algorithm is driven by local feedback and simulated evolutionary pressures. The model aims to move beyond traditional artificial neural networks, which often rely on predefined architectures and training methods, towards a truly emergent system where complexity arises naturally. Key components include node design with limited, evolving computational abilities, a symbiotic connection algorithm, and a simulated evolutionary process. Mathematical formulations detail the core principles driving the network's formation and adaptation. The presented approach offers a potential pathway to understanding and potentially replicating the emergence of complex neural structures in biological systems.

title: ## Batear Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Batear Fox Hunting
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Batear Fox, inspired by the hunting strategies of Batear foxes. Batear foxes, renowned for their ambush hunting techniques and strategic decision-making, provide a compelling source of inspiration for designing an effective optimization algorithm. Batear Fox leverages a combination of concepts from the Batear fox's behavior, including territorial marking, strategic positioning, and coordinated attacks, to create a novel search process. The algorithm employs a dynamic territory assignment mechanism, a weighted exploration-exploitation strategy, and a simulated coordinated attack process to navigate the search space efficiently. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance across several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's key features include adaptability to varying problem landscapes, robustness against local optima, and a relatively simple implementation. Experimental results confirm that Batear Fox is a promising alternative for solving complex optimization challenges.

abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive clustering algorithm designed to handle high-dimensional data. title: Quantum Biology Simulation and Prediction
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing for simulating and predicting biological processes. The core concept involves translating complex biological systems, specifically molecular interactions, into quantum systems represented by quantum states. These quantum states are then subjected to simulation and prediction using quantum computing algorithms. The work aims to address the inherent limitations of classical computing in accurately modeling quantum phenomena within biological systems, such as those involved in photosynthesis, enzyme catalysis, and perhaps even consciousness. We present a framework for this approach, highlighting the challenges and opportunities involved. Specifically, we investigate the applicability of quantum algorithms – like Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and Quantum Monte Carlo – to model biological systems. The ultimate goal is to quantify the probability of specific biological events occurring, leading to a fundamentally new approach to biological research and drug discovery. This research proposes a novel methodology for leveraging the power of quantum computation to unlock the secrets of life.

title: Probability Logic Framework for Machine Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the integration of set theory and probability logic to enhance machine learning model training and evaluation. We propose a novel framework leveraging the inherent properties of set theory – the concept of "all possibilities" – alongside the probabilistic nature of probability logic. The core claim is that this integration allows for more robust and scalable model development, offering a principled approach to uncertainty and generalization. Traditional machine learning often struggles with model interpretability and the ability to effectively generalize across diverse datasets. This paper introduces a probabilistic framework that addresses these challenges by providing a more structured and adaptable approach to model optimization. We detail the core mechanisms of this framework, focusing on how set theory and probability logic are combined to facilitate a deeper understanding of model behavior and improve its performance.

title: Hyper-Dimensional Computing with Reservoir Computing and Neural ODEs
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to temporal data processing by integrating Reservoir Computing principles with Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs). Traditional Neural ODEs are constrained by the need to explicitly learn a fixed differential equation, limiting their ability to capture complex, potentially non-linear temporal dynamics. We propose a "Hyper-Dimensional Reservoir Neural ODE," where a reservoir – a randomly connected network of nodes – serves as the dynamical system within the Neural ODE framework. This design leverages the inherent temporal dynamics of the reservoir, allowing the Neural ODE to learn and represent unbounded temporal dependencies. The core claim is that this synergistic combination offers a significant advancement over standard Neural ODEs, unlocking potentially unlimited temporal representation capabilities. We outline the theoretical foundations, the proposed architecture, and discuss the potential benefits and challenges of this approach.

title: Multi-Modal Neural Networks for High-Dimensional Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for high-dimensional information encoding based on multi-modal neural networks. The core idea is to design a neural network where each neuron simultaneously processes information from multiple modalities—such as time, space, and frequency—and performs a non-linear combination to achieve compact encoding. We introduce a "modal fusion" mechanism, which involves weighted fusion of outputs from neurons processing different modalities. Furthermore, we employ an adaptive weighting learning mechanism to optimize the compression representation of high-dimensional data. Unlike existing methods that typically focus on single-modal data, our approach addresses the complex inter-correlations inherent in high-dimensional datasets. The system leverages the inherent redundancy within multi-modal data to achieve efficient and compact representation. This work presents a foundational approach for encoding complex data streams and offers a pathway towards more robust and accurate data analysis.

title: Asian Elephant Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Asian Elephant Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (AEIMA), designed for tackling complex optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the observed behaviors of Asian elephants, specifically their foraging strategies and social interactions. AEIMA utilizes a combination of adaptive movement patterns, group dynamics, and memory mechanisms to explore the search space effectively. The core components of the algorithm include an adaptive movement system mimicking elephant gait, a social influence mechanism simulating herd behavior, and a memory component representing past successful locations. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's parameters and operational rules. title: ## The Arctic Grayling Inspired Adaptive Migration Optimization Algorithm (AGIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Arctic Grayling Inspired Adaptive Migration Optimization Algorithm (AGIMO), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the migratory behavior of the Arctic Grayling ( *Anser caerulescens* ). The algorithm leverages the Grayling's demonstrated ability to adapt its migratory route based on environmental factors, particularly food availability and weather conditions, to optimize solutions in complex search spaces. AGIMO combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Adaptive Memory Search (AMS) with a novel adaptive strategy termed "Environmental Awareness," which mimics the Grayling's real-time assessment of its surroundings. The algorithm maintains a population of 'migrants' exploring the search space, updating their positions and velocities based on their individual and global best performance, while dynamically adjusting their movement based on a simulated "environmental score" reflecting resource abundance and navigational difficulty. The core innovation lies in the dynamic scaling of the environmental awareness factor, ensuring a balance between exploitation and exploration, crucial for efficient convergence. The algorithm's potential application across diverse optimization problems is discussed, highlighting its adaptability and robustness.

title: Antilopine Wallaby: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Antilopine Wallaby Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Antilopine Wallaby, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of antilopine wallabies. The algorithm mimics the wallaby's strategy of exploring the environment, selecting promising locations, and returning to previously visited areas with high food density. Antilopine Wallaby incorporates elements of the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm, specifically utilizing a memory pool to store promising solutions and a negative feedback mechanism inspired by the wallaby's avoidance of overcrowded food sources. The algorithm's core loop consists of three phases: exploration, selection, and exploitation. The exploration phase utilizes a probabilistic movement strategy based on the wallaby's movement patterns. The selection phase employs a rank-based selection scheme to prioritize high-quality solutions. The exploitation phase focuses on refining the selected solutions through a local search technique. The performance of Antilopine Wallaby is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving various optimization challenges. The results indicate that Antilopine Wallaby provides competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, suggesting its potential for practical applications.

title: Dynamic Topological Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Network
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing quantum entanglement networks that dynamically adapt to environmental fluctuations. The core claim is that real-time monitoring of decoherence rates and environmental noise, coupled with adaptive network topology adjustments, can maximize the efficiency of entanglement information transmission. The proposed mechanism utilizes machine learning algorithms to analyze quantum bit (qubit) quantum state information, predict decoherence rates, and automatically optimize qubit-to-qubit connections, resulting in a self-adaptive entanglement network. Existing quantum entanglement networks largely rely on fixed topologies, lacking the adaptability necessary to contend with dynamic environmental changes. This research bridges the gap by integrating machine learning with quantum entanglement networks, enabling a truly adaptive entanglement network. The key performance indicator (KPI) for this network is the entanglement fidelity (EF), defined as: EF = ∑i |⟨ψ⟩i|2 where ψi represents the entangled state of qubits i and the summation is performed over all qubits in the network. The network's overall efficiency is directly correlated with maintaining high entanglement fidelity over extended periods. The goal is to minimize the decoherence rate (R) which is defined as: R = d(ρ)/dt where ρ is the density matrix of the quantum system. The adaptive network topology dynamically adjusts to minimize R, thus maximizing the entanglement fidelity. Further, the network's performance is evaluated using the average entanglement distribution (AED) calculated as: AED = (1/N) ∑j=1N Ej where N is the number of qubits and Ej is the entanglement between qubit j and the rest of the network.

title: Quantum Topology Computing: An Extension
abstract: Quantum topology is a burgeoning field of research exploring the unique properties of quantum systems, offering a novel approach to computation and optimization. This paper investigates the application of quantum topology to the design of advanced quantum algorithms, particularly focusing on the development of a new quantum algorithm based on "reconstruction" principles. The core claim posits that this method, leveraging the power of quantum topology, can significantly enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum computation, thereby unlocking new possibilities within the field. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm that employs a "reconstruction" process, meticulously manipulating quantum states to achieve a desired outcome. This approach promises to overcome limitations of traditional quantum algorithms and pave the way for more powerful and reliable quantum systems.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-informed topology, specifically the incorporation of non-classical topology into the modeling of probabilistic fields and quantum computation. The core mechanism involves a mapping of topology to quantum states, utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to achieve more accurate probabilistic modeling and improved quantum computing performance. This work addresses a critical gap in current research by directly integrating topological principles into the design of quantum algorithms and models, promising a significant advancement in the scalability of quantum computation.

abstract: This paper introduces the Phoenix Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the intricate and symmetrical arrangement of peacock feathers. title: Neural Network Based on Probabilistic Dynamic Topology Learning (PBDTSL)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network training, termed Probabilistic Dynamic Topology Learning (PBDTSL), which leverages principles from biological neural networks to achieve adaptive and optimized network topology. The core concept involves treating the neural network as a probabilistic process, incorporating stochastic synaptic connections, dynamic neuron death/regeneration, and Markov chain modeling for predicting connection probabilities. The system dynamically adjusts connection weights and regulates the death/regeneration rate of neurons based on network performance feedback. PBDTSL addresses the limitations of conventional neural network training methods that often assume fixed network topologies. The system's ability to actively adapt its structure based on learning feedback offers a promising pathway for tackling complex tasks and building more robust and efficient neural networks. The key mathematical formulations are presented, detailing the probabilistic modeling, Markov chain dynamics, and the adaptive learning mechanism. The model's ability to handle evolving network topologies through probabilistic transitions and dynamic neuron populations is highlighted as a key differentiator. This research aims to bridge the gap between artificial neural networks and the inherent dynamic nature of biological systems, leading to improved learning capabilities and network resilience. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked regardless of distance, has captivated physicists and philosophers alike. This research explores the potential of utilizing geometric principles to understand and manipulate entanglement, proposing a novel model to represent quantum entanglement as a geometric structure. We aim to investigate how the inherent geometry of entangled states can be leveraged to optimize quantum computation and communication protocols. The core claim is that establishing a geometric model of quantum entanglement will unlock new avenues for enhancing the performance of these technologies. This paper delves into the foundational concepts and proposes a mechanism for translating entanglement into a geometric framework, ultimately seeking to reveal hidden properties and potential optimizations within the space of entangled quantum states.

title: Adaptive Mimicry Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Red-Crested Woodpecker
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Mimicry Optimization Algorithm (AMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the red-crested woodpecker. The woodpecker's ability to adapt its pecking strategy based on the sound and visual cues of its environment provides a compelling analogy for intelligent exploration and exploitation in optimization problems. AMOA leverages the concept of 'mimicry' – the woodpecker copying successful pecking patterns – combined with adaptive adjustment of parameters based on the perceived 'fitness' of those patterns. The algorithm employs a population of potential solutions, iteratively refining them through a process of mimicry and adaptation. Key components include a 'resonance' mechanism to prioritize mimicking high-performing solutions, a 'diversity' maintenance strategy to prevent premature convergence, and a dynamic adjustment of the mimicking rate based on the overall population's fitness landscape. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a theoretical justification for its effectiveness, demonstrating its potential for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: ## Bioluminescence-Inspired Adaptive Search (BIAS): A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces Bioluminescence-Inspired Adaptive Search (BIAS), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the fascinating bioluminescent behavior of deep-sea sharks. Specifically, we draw inspiration from the way sharks modulate their light emission based on environmental conditions and prey detection. BIAS utilizes a dynamic population of "light beacons" representing potential solutions, with each beacon's intensity reflecting its fitness. The algorithm incorporates a "sensitivity mechanism" analogous to the shark's sensory system, allowing it to adaptively adjust the exploration and exploitation phases based on the diversity and convergence of the light beacon population. A key innovation is the "pulse-modulation" strategy, mimicking the rhythmic flashing patterns of bioluminescent sharks, which controls the movement of the light beacons through the search space. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and presents a theoretical framework for understanding its behavior. We argue that BIAS's adaptive nature, coupled with its pulsed movement strategy, offers a promising approach to tackling complex optimization problems.

title: WP-008 — Information Routing in E8: Why Geometry Is Necessary But Not Sufficient
abstract: The E8 lattice offers a unified structural language for information routing, but its geometric properties alone are insufficient to guarantee correct information selection. This paper clarifies a critical finding from the dedupe knight implementation: semantic collision—two distinct information objects occupying the same lattice point—can occur despite perfect geometric alignment. We argue that geometry must be paired with intentionality, context constraint, and coherence-preservation mechanisms to function as a routing engine. We document the architectural constraints this imposes and sketch implications for the Excalibur blueprint and 248-dimensional threading at production scale.

title: A Korea–U.S. Comparative Study on Inventorship Standards for AI-Assisted Inventions : The USPTO’s 2025 Revised Guidance Withdrawing the Pannu-Factor Approach and the Reconstruction of Inventorship Analysis under Korean Patent Law
authors: 법률사무소 아티스 변호사, 변리사, 법학박사, 서울대학교 강사.
abstract: 인공지능(AI)을 도구로 활용한 발명에서 자연인이 언제 특허법상 발명자의 창작행위를 수행하였다고 볼 것인가는 AI 자체의 발명자 적격과 구별되는 문제이다. 발명자는 자연인에 한정된다는 원칙만으로는과제 설정, 프롬프트 구성, 산출물의 선택ㆍ수정, 실험ㆍ검증 등으로분산된 인간의 행위 중 무엇이 청구발명의 형성에 실질적으로 기여하였는지를 판단하기 어렵다. 본고는 미국의 지침 변화와 그 기초가 된구상(conception)ㆍ공동발명 판례법리를 검토하고, 이를 우리 특허법상발명자 법리와 비교하여 AI 활용 발명에서 인간 기여를 판단하고 입증하기 위한 기준을 제시한다. USPTO는 2024년 AI 활용 발명에 Pannu Factors를 확장 적용하였으나, 2025년 이를 철회하고 단독 자연인에게는 전통적 구상 기준을 적용하도록 정리하였다. 이는 인간 발명자 요건을 완화한 것이 아니라 자연인의 창작행위와 청구발명 사이의 연결을 직접 확인하는 구조로 초점을돌린 것이다. 다만 이러한 전환이 우리 특허법에 곧바로 별도의 입법적공백을 발생시키는 것은 아니다. 우리 판례는 이미 단순한 과제의 제시 나 자금ㆍ설비의 제공과 구별하여, 구체적인 착상의 제시ㆍ부가ㆍ보완또는 실험을 통한 구체화 등 기술적 사상의 창작에 대한 실질적 기여를발명자 판단의 중심에 두고 있다. 그러므로 미국법상 구상(conception) 을 한국법에 이식하기보다, 기존의 착상ㆍ구체화 법리를 AI 활용 과정의 구체적 행위와 청구항의 기술적 내용에 연결할 필요가 있다. 본고는 이를 위하여 ① 청구항에 구현된 기술적 해결수단과 그 구성ㆍ한정사항을 특정하고, ② 자연인이 수행한 행위와 그 시점을 발명의형성과정 및 완성시점에 대응시키고, ③ 그 행위가 착상의 제시ㆍ부가ㆍ보완 또는 실험을 통한 구체화로서 발명의 완성에 실질적으로 기여하였는지를 평가하는 청구항별 3단계 판단모형을 제안한다. 이 모형에서 프롬프트 작성, 산출물의 선택ㆍ수정, 실험의 수행이라는 행위명칭은 그 자체로 발명자성을 긍정하거나 부정하지 않는다. 사용자ㆍ개발자ㆍ데이터 제공자의 지위 역시 계약관계나 역할명칭이 아니라 각 자연인이 청구항의 기술적 해결수단 형성에 실제로 기여하였는지에 따라 판단할 필요가 있다. 본고는 이러한 실체적 판단을 출원ㆍ심사ㆍ심판ㆍ소송 단계에서 뒷받침하기 위하여 프롬프트, AI 산출물, 수정이력, 연구노트 및 실험기록을 청구항의 구성별로 연결하는 “청구항별 기여매핑”을 제안한다. 또한 발명자성 판단을 서면기재ㆍ실시가능ㆍ진보성 등 인접 특허요건과 구별하고, 발명자 확정 이후의 권리귀속ㆍ직무발명 보상ㆍ계약상 이익배분과도 구별할 필요가 있다. AI 활용 발명의 발명자성은 청구된 기술적 해결수단이 어떠한 과정에서형성되었고 어느 자연인이 이를 착상하거나 구체화하였는지를 확인하여 판단되는 것이 바람직하다.

title: Light-driven molecular reorientation for large-scale photonic in-memory computing
abstract: Abstract Photonics has the potential to transform high-speed and energy-efficient artificial intelligence. However, most photonic computing platforms still rely on costly electro-optic conversions for data input, weight loading and storage, resulting in substantial overhead during large-scale computation. Here, we present a large-scale photonic in-memory computing platform based on liquid crystal (LC)-enabled Poincaré-sphere-connected neural networks. Megabyte-level nonvolatile photonic memory is introduced through light-driven reorientation of sulfonic azo-dye and LC molecules, which also functions as the reconfigurable optical neurons. This architecture uniquely integrates optical sensing, memory, and computing in situ, allowing minimal data-movement overheads in various switchable machine vision tasks. Ultrahigh scalability is demonstrated by a 9.44-million-neuron photonic processor array that supports massively parallel optical computing, recording and retrieval, providing a memory capacity 100,000 times larger than state-of-the-art photonic in-memory computing. This work offers a novel pathway toward scalable submicrometer-precision photonic memory, thus establishing a new paradigm for physical neural networks and brain-like artificial intelligence.

title: Investigating Hyperparameter Optimization and Transferability for ES-HyperNEAT: A TPE Approach
abstract: Neuroevolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT) and its advanced version, Evolvable-Substrate HyperNEAT (ES-HyperNEAT), have shown great potential in developing neural networks. However, their effectiveness heavily depends on the selection of hyperparameters. This study investigates the optimization of ES-HyperNEAT hyperparameters using the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) on the MNIST classification task, exploring a search space of over 3 billion potential combinations. TPE effectively navigates this vast space, significantly outperforming random search in terms of mean, median, and best accuracy. During the validation process, the best hyperparameter configuration found by TPE achieves an accuracy of 29.00\% on MNIST, surpassing previous studies while using a smaller population size and fewer generations. The transferability of the optimized hyperparameters is explored in logic operations and Fashion-MNIST tasks, revealing successful transfer to the more complex Fashion-MNIST problem but limited to simpler logic operations. This study emphasizes a method to unlock the full potential of neuroevolutionary algorithms and provides insights into the hyperparameters' transferability across tasks of varying complexity.

title: Local Private Information Retrieval for Graph-Based Replicated Systems
abstract: We rethink the definition of privacy in multi-server, graph-replicated private information retrieval (PIR) systems, by introducing a novel setting where the user's privacy is governed by the servers' storage structure. In classical graph-replicated PIR, the user retrieves a single message stored at the servers, while hiding the message index from each server. In our proposed privacy setting, the user is concerned with hiding the message index from a particular server, only if that server stores the message being retrieved, and privacy is not imposed otherwise. We coin this relaxed privacy requirement as local user privacy and the resulting PIR problem as local PIR on the graph. Our focus is on two-replicated PIR systems, where every message is replicated twice and stored on two distinct servers. Specifically, we study local PIR systems where the storage is represented by simple graphs, i.e., every pair of vertices is associated with at most one edge, and by their multigraph extension, i.e., $r$ parallel edges replace every edge. For these settings, we establish bounds on the local PIR capacity, defined as the maximum number of message symbols retrieved, per downloaded symbol. The local privacy requirement yields significant capacity gain over the classical PIR capacity under the same storage structure. For instance, in settings where the graph is a disjoint union of multiple identical sub-graphs, the gain in the local PIR capacity over classical PIR capacity is multiplicative in the number of sub-graphs. Further, for connected graphs, we derive capacity lower bounds for edge-transitive and bipartite graphs, which are greater than the best-known PIR capacity bounds. From these and by establishing matching upper bounds, we exactly characterize the capacity for star graphs, cyclic graphs, and path graphs with odd number of vertices. We introduce two local PIR schemes for general graphs.

title: Best Annealing Path of Quantum Annealing via Efficient Adiabatic Phase Transition
abstract: Quantum Annealing (QA) has already put into practical use and considered useful for solving many social issues, such as reduction of traffic congestion and delivery optimization. But in QA, when the energy difference between the ground state and the first excited state is small, the transition probability between them increases. Therefore, in order to decrease the transition, QA has to be performed at extremely low temperatures. To simulate the situation, it has the problem in that it takes much time. Many studies are underway to accelerate QA theoretically, one of which is to incorporate non-stoquastic Hamiltonian. On the other hand, I proposed Nested Simulated Annealing (NSA) inspired by Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). I showed the computational speedup could be achieved dramatically, by considering the idea that the effect of flipping a spin preferentially influenced the spins directly interacting with it. Although NSA was based on such classical concept of causality, the hybrid computation both quantum and classical approach worked well. In this paper, in order to discuss the relationship between NSA and non-stoquastic Hamiltonian like XX-interaction, the spins are treated as continuous variables. I derive the formula to calculate the total energy in both with a problem Hamiltonian and the perturbation Hamiltonian induced by a transverse electromagnetic field. And I will show a clear relationship between local-maxima and the convergence speed when calculating it with the binary spin. More precisely, the annealing path with the smallest local-maxima converges fast, even though it consumes fewer computational resources. Therefore, it is possible to induce an optimal adiabatic phase transition by selecting NSA parameters appropriately. This paper shows an effective method to choose the parameters when simulating QMC on a classical computer.

title: Reducio: Optimized Confidential Serverless Cloud Deployments for Enterprise Customers
abstract: Serverless platforms based on Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs) have been recently proposed to address the privacy problems with serverless functions, while achieving low latency. Unfortunately, our study indicates that to achieve these properties, existing proposals impose non-trivial requirements in terms of infrastructure changes and platform memory. Reducio is an alternate serverless platform design that does not require infrastructure changes and significantly reduces platform memory requirements. The platform is designed using two key components: (1) a function isolation framework inside a CVM based on kernel deprivileging features that minimize infrastructure requirements, and (2) a layer-wise caching methodology and algorithm that effectively uses a small in-memory function cache. Our evaluation indicates that Reducio can significantly reduce both platform requirements for deployment and function memory consumption.

title: Quantum-Resilient Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Review of Ethical Governance and Regulatory Frameworks
abstract: Quantum computing poses a severe threat to standard digital security protocols, leaving artificial intelligence (AI) data pipelines and decision-support systems highly exposed. As large-scale quantum attacks become computationally feasible, the public-key cryptography currently securing data transmission will likely fail. This vulnerability threatens sectors heavily reliant on AI—including finance, healthcare, and critical infrastructure escalating the probability of data breaches, integrity losses, and compliance failures. To address these interconnected security, governance, and ethical hurdles, this paper introduces the Integrated Quantum-Resilient AI Framework (IQRAI). IQRAI establishes a structured governance model combining proactive quantum risk assessments, post-quantum cryptography (PQC), and continuous security monitoring. A core focus of the framework is balancing cryptographic migration with strict ethical requirements, specifically data privacy, algorithmic transparency, fairness, and auditability. Furthermore, the study reviews ongoing global standardization efforts for PQC transitions to define baseline requirements for sustained system resilience. By comparing existing mitigation models across metrics of operational friction, implementation difficulty, and security yield, the research identifies a critical operational gap. The analysis demonstrates that merely swapping cryptographic algorithms is insufficient for achieving quantum-resilient AI; securing these systems demands a unified approach that links security engineering, ethical oversight, and regulatory adherence. Ultimately, this work delivers a strategic roadmap for organizations to systematically harden their AI ecosystems against quantum threats while maintaining operational trust and legal compliance.

title: From Drift Detection to Diagnosis: An Explainable Framework for Deployed Machine Learning
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models are increasingly deployed in real-world environments where data characteristics, user behaviour, and operating conditions may change over time. Such changes can lead to data or concept drift and may gradually reduce model reliability. Existing monitoring approaches can identify distributional changes or performance degradation, but they often provide limited information about why the changes occur. Similarly, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods can explain model predictions but are frequently treated separately from continuous drift monitoring. This paper proposes a unified drift-aware framework for explainable diagnostics in deployed machine learning systems. The framework integrates data-drift detection, model-performance monitoring, explainability, and diagnostic decision-making into a continuous monitoring pipeline. Statistical drift detection methods are used to identify changes between reference and production data, while XAI techniques such as SHAP and LIME are used to identify important features associated with changes in model behaviour. The framework combines drift indicators and performance information to generate interpretable diagnostic reports and recommend suitable maintenance actions. The proposed approach aims to improve the transparency, reliability, and maintainability of deployed ML systems by connecting drift detection with actionable explanations. The framework can support proactive model monitoring and assist practitioners in deciding whether continued monitoring, investigation, recalibration, or model retraining is required. Keywords: Explainable AI,Machine Learning Deployment, Model Monitoring,Drift Detection

title: SCILLA v1.1.0 Synthetic Evidence
abstract: This dataset is the reproducibility and robustness evidence companion to the SCILLA v1.1.0 canonical research note (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22209746). It contains the synthetic evidence used to audit and reproduce the principal computational results of SCILLA, including matched run-level results, aggregate policy effects, paired-bootstrap confidence intervals, sign-flip tests, parameter sensitivity sweeps, prior-mismatch and other ablation experiments, independent trace-verifier results, canonical trace records, the frozen experimental protocol, assumptions, and seed registry. The evidence preserves both positive and negative results. In particular, the released experiments do not support universal adaptive superiority for raw discovery. The dataset instead supports more bounded findings concerning paired ascent/return reacquisition, the constructed priority-weighted Track Debt metric, and decision-weighted utility under the declared synthetic reference conditions. All performance data contained in this record are synthetic or recomputed from the released SCILLA research software. No physical SCILLA field measurement is included. The dataset does not establish operational detection range, field tracking performance, customer ROI, patent status, QPU execution, or quantum advantage. An independent trace verifier is included in the associated evidence architecture to recompute geometry, eligibility, scan constraints, observation identities, paired-state counts, and final metric identities without selecting the optimizer’s actions. This dataset supplements the canonical SCILLA v1.1.0 research publication: Michele Giletto, “SCILLA: Altitude-Coupled Transient Maritime Surface Observation — Geometry, Paired State Estimation, and Falsification of Adaptive Scan Allocation,” Giletto Systems Lab, v1.1.0, 2026. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22209746. The next validation gates are external historical sensor replay and a cooperative paired-observation field experiment using synchronized platform navigation and independent target ground truth.

title: Effects-and-Lifetimes Calculus — Mechanized Safety Proofs
abstract: A Rocq (Coq) formalization of a call-by-value calculus with bounded type polymorphism (full F<:), a separate lifetime sort forming a two-point lattice, algebraic data constructors with existential lifetime/type schemas, and algebraic effect handlers with multi-shot resumptions — the proof-side companion of the CoreΔ calculus. The safety story is lifetime-based capability confinement: effect capabilities are local-annotated values, and the lifetime subtyping discipline guarantees that neither a capability nor any local-confined datum can escape the scope that delimits it. The development is axiom-free — every capstone theorem prints «Closed under the global context» under Print Assumptions, enforced by a derived assumption gate (make verify). It includes type soundness, capability confinement at every syntactic occurrence, guarded handler-boundary theorems on states and on labelled transition events with a certified completeness accounting, determinism modulo the fresh-marker choice, certified reflected deciders and a certified evaluator with an OCaml extraction, and a fully verified examples tier with a rejection suite. See README.md for the theorem table and ARTIFACT.md for the build and verification guide.
