title: VIBE: Video Instruction-aligned Background music gEneration
abstract: Current video-to-music (V2M) models lack semantic control and fail to penalize instruction violations, largely due to their reliance on reconstruction objectives and the representational bottleneck of static cross-modal conditioning in Diffusion Autoregressive (DAR) architectures. To resolve this, we introduce VIBE, a novel text-and-video-to-music (T+V2M) generation model that leverages: (1) Conditioning Connection, a depth-wise cross-layer conditioning mechanism that dynamically bridges the planning and diffusion refinement heads and (2) a comprehensive reward modeling taxonomy, optimizing for both hard, verifiable constraints (e.g., tempo, key) and soft, subjective qualities (e.g., musicality, multimodal alignment) with a structured 5-stage training curriculum. Upon evaluation using audio-visual alignment, instruction following, and audio quality metrics, along with a subjective human evaluation study, we observe that VIBE demonstrates enhanced controllability and instruction adherence while performing comparably to most evaluated baselines on generation fidelity and multimodal alignment.

title: Ampere: Communication-Efficient and High-Accuracy Split Federated Learning
abstract: A Federated Learning (FL) system collaboratively trains neural networks across devices and a server but is limited by significant on-device computation costs. Split Federated Learning (SFL) systems mitigate this by offloading a block of layers of the network from the device to a server. However, in doing so, it introduces large communication overheads due to frequent exchanges of intermediate activations and gradients between devices and the server and reduces model accuracy for non-IID data. We propose Ampere, a novel collaborative training system that simultaneously minimizes on-device computation and device-server communication while improving model accuracy. Unlike SFL, which uses a global loss by iterative end-to-end training, Ampere develops unidirectional inter-block training to sequentially train the device and server blocks with a local loss, eliminating the transfer of gradients. A lightweight auxiliary network generation method decouples training between the device and server, reducing frequent intermediate exchanges to a single transfer, which significantly reduces the communication overhead. Ampere mitigates the impact of data heterogeneity by consolidating activations generated by the trained device block to train the server block, in contrast to SFL, which trains on device-specific, non-IID activations. Extensive experiments on multiple CNNs and Transformers show that, compared to state-of-the-art SFL baseline systems, Ampere (i) improves model accuracy by up to 11.70 percentage points while training up to 18.6x faster, (ii) incurs up to 911x lower device-server communication overhead and up to 14.5x lower on-device computation, and (iii) reduces standard deviation of accuracy by 71.13% for various non-IID degrees highlighting superior performance when faced with heterogeneous data. Ampere is available from https://github.com/blessonvar/Ampere.

title: ANALISIS PENERAPAN TOMEK LINKS SEBAGAI METODE PEMBERSIH DAN SMOTE UNTUK MENGATASI KETIDAKSEIMBANGAN KELAS PADA KLASIFIKASI HUJAN
abstract: Latar belakang. Hujan memiliki pengaruh yang besar terhadap kehidupan dan aktivitas manusia, maka dari itu hujan dengan frekuensi yang sangat tinggi dapat menyebabkan bencana alam, merusak ekosistem dan menyebabkan masalah pada berbagai bidang. Klasifikasi hujan yang akurat dapat membantu dalam pengambilan keputusan serta dalam mempersiapkan diri untuk meningkatkan kesiagaan dalam menghadapi masalah ataupun bencana alam yang dapat terjadi akibat hujan, Model klasifikasi yang akurat dipengaruhi oleh kualitas dan keseimbangan kelas yang digunakan saat proses pelatihan Tujuan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh teknik resampling dalam mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas maupun metode pembersihan data serta menganalisis urutan penerapan kedua metode tersebut terhadap kinerja klasifikasi hujan. Metode. Metode yang diusulkan pada penelitian ini yaitu Tomek Links sebagai metode pembersih data yang ambigu dan tumpeng tindih dan SMOTE sebagai teknik resampling dalam mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas, yang dijabarkan dalam beberapa skenario untuk dianalisis lebih lanjut. Hasil. Berdasarkan perbandingan eksperimen, penerapan Tomek Links sebagai metode pembersih yang diikuti oleh SMOTE untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas pada model memberikan kinerja tertinggi dengan akurasi sebesar 93%, recall sebesar 92,66%, presisi sebesar 93,31% dan f1-score sebesar 92.97%. Kesimpulan. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa penanganan ketidakseimbangan kelas dan pembersihan data dan juga urutan penerapannya efektif dalam meningkatkan kinerja klasifikasi hujan, serta menunjukkan bahwa urutan penerapan Tomek Links diikuti oleh SMOTE merupakan pendekatan yang paling optimal dibandingkan skenario lainnya.

title: Using GBIF RDF to find applicable taxonomic literature
abstract: Recently, after the wonderful work of Andra Waagmeester, Jerven Bolleman, and Hannah Bast, an RDF version of the data on the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) was made available through a SPARQL endpoint on QLever. Roderic Page writes about it in iPhylo : Now, it just so happens that the Library of Identification Resources (LoIR) is available as an RDF dataset.

title: Analisis Sentimen Dual-Channel Opini Publik Terhadap Pajak dan MBG Berbasis Indobert
abstract: Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) memicu diskursus fiskal intens di platform X, namun penelitian terdahulu belum memisahkan kritik pendanaan dari aspek urgensi gizi. Penelitian ini mengusulkan model Dual-Channel Tematik yang memadukan Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) untuk pemetaan topik dan IndoBERT (fine-tuned) untuk klasifikasi sentimen tiga kelas. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan model IndoBERT dengan class weighting mencapai akurasi 80,23% dan F1-score makro 0,659. Pemodelan LDA berhasil memetakan dua klaster tematik: Pajak/Fiskal (183 komentar) dan Urgensi/Gizi (243 komentar). Sentimen positif lebih dominan pada topik Urgensi/Gizi (77,4%), sedangkan sentimen negatif lebih tinggi pada topik Pajak/Fiskal (13,7%). Meskipun demikian, uji chi-square menunjukkan hubungan antara topik dan sentimen tidak signifikan secara statistik (χ^2=3,531; p=0,171). Penelitian ini memberikan diagnosis komputasi awal yang berkontribusi sebagai dasar perumusan komunikasi kebijakan MBG yang lebih tepat sasaran.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Geometric Optimization – Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a unique paradigm for computational exploration, potentially enabling breakthroughs in complex optimization problems. This paper explores the design of a novel geometric optimization algorithm leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced precision and efficiency. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters using entangled qubit states, allowing for a fundamentally different optimization process compared to classical methods. The core mechanism centers around the exploitation of entanglement to create a parallel exploration of the solution space, resulting in a more robust and adaptable optimization strategy. The research investigates the potential of this algorithm to tackle challenging geometric optimization tasks, specifically focusing on the design of a self-adaptive system for parameter tuning within complex shapes. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical implications and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy.

title: Dynamic Scalable Quantum Computing (DCQC) Framework
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, offering unparalleled computational power and enabling breakthroughs in areas like drug discovery, materials science, and financial modeling. However, current quantum algorithms often struggle to achieve optimal performance due to the difficulty of accurately controlling and tuning quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel dynamic-adaptive quantum computing framework, termed Dynamic Scalable Quantum Computing (DCQC), which dynamically adjusts quantum system parameters based on the quantum computation's current state. title: Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) for Anomaly Detection in Time Series
abstract: This paper explores the application of Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) to the challenging problem of anomaly detection in time series data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with the complexity and inherent variability found in real-world time series. HTM, originally developed for predictive coding and pattern recognition, offers a fundamentally different approach by learning hierarchical representations of temporal patterns. This work presents a framework for adapting HTM principles to time series anomaly detection, focusing on the use of "stocks" and "sequences" to capture and maintain temporal dependencies. The core claim is that HTM's ability to learn local patterns can be effectively leveraged to identify anomalies when these patterns are disrupted. We detail a system designed specifically for time series, outlining the key components and operational principles. The system learns by creating a hierarchy of temporal patterns, allowing for robust detection of deviations from the norm. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the potential of this approach, highlighting its ability to capture complex temporal relationships and identify subtle anomalies that might be missed by conventional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the broader implications of HTM for time series analysis.

title: Causal Discovery from Observational Data using Bayesian Networks with Dynamic Structure Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery from observational data utilizing dynamic Bayesian networks. Traditional Bayesian network structure learning methods often assume static datasets, failing to capture evolving causal relationships encountered in dynamic environments. Our methodology addresses this limitation by incorporating a dynamic structure learning algorithm that continuously adapts the Bayesian network's topology and parameter estimates as new data streams arrive. We leverage a variational inference technique to efficiently maintain probabilistic representations throughout this adaptation process. The core innovation lies in the iterative refinement of the network structure, allowing it to accurately represent causal dependencies that may shift over time. This approach offers a robust solution for causal discovery in scenarios where the underlying data distribution is not stationary, a common characteristic of many real-world applications. The system is designed to provide a more accurate understanding of causal relationships compared to static Bayesian network approaches, significantly improving decision-making capabilities in dynamic systems. The presented method is scalable and can handle large datasets, offering a practical solution for complex causal inference problems.

title: Self-Organizing Hierarchical Neural Networks for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic reasoning using self-organizing hierarchical neural networks. The core idea is that neural networks can learn hierarchical symbolic representations through a competitive self-organization process, analogous to how humans develop cognitive structures. Unlike traditional backpropagation, which relies on gradient descent to adjust weights, this method leverages competition between multiple layers of neural networks. Each layer attempts to represent a particular level of abstraction, and the winning representation propagates to deeper layers, effectively building a hierarchy. We formalize this mechanism with equations that describe the competitive learning process and the propagation of information. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and interpretable way to achieve symbolic reasoning compared to current deep learning methods. The architecture is described in detail, and the key equations are presented to illustrate the core principles. The research demonstrates the potential of this approach for tasks requiring hierarchical understanding and reasoning.

title: Black Saki: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Black Sakis
abstract: This paper presents Black Saki, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies employed by Black Sakis (Lemur fulvus), a species of lemur endemic to Madagascar. Black Sakis are renowned for their unique, highly efficient foraging techniques, particularly their ability to locate and exploit food resources in complex and dynamic environments. Black Saki leverages these observed behaviors to create a new algorithm for solving optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates elements of Lévy flight, clustered searching, and a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Black Saki through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and the Powell's test functions. Results indicate that Black Saki exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of animal behavior—specifically, the foraging patterns of Black Sakis—as a source of inspiration for algorithm design, offering a potentially robust and adaptable approach to optimization.

title: Formal Modeling of Trust in Federated Learning Systems using Game Theory
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising approach to distributed machine learning, enabling model training across multiple devices without direct data sharing. However, the inherent decentralized nature of FL introduces significant challenges regarding trust, security, and privacy. Currently, the design and analysis of effective trust mechanisms within FL systems are largely reliant on informal assumptions and heuristics, leaving systems vulnerable to malicious actors and strategic behavior. This paper presents a rigorous, game-theoretic model to formally analyze trust dynamics in FL systems. The model captures the strategic interactions between clients (data providers) and a central server, explicitly incorporating trust, reputation, and incentive mechanisms. Through this framework, we can quantitatively assess the impact of various trust-building strategies and identify potential vulnerabilities. The model's ability to represent and analyze these complex interactions provides a foundation for designing robust and reliable FL systems. We explore scenarios where trust evolves based on participant behavior, highlighting the importance of reputation systems and incentive alignment for optimal system performance. The key contributions of this work are a formal mathematical representation of trust dynamics in FL, a framework for analyzing strategic interactions, and insights into designing effective trust mechanisms to mitigate risks.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Routing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to network routing leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional network routing relies on physical distances and delays, presenting inherent limitations in bandwidth and latency. This research posits that quantum entanglement can be harnessed to overcome these constraints, enabling ultra-high bandwidth and low-latency data routing. The core concept involves constructing a "quantum network" composed of entangled qubits, enabling efficient data transmission and routing via precise control of the entangled states. We explore and develop algorithms designed to minimize entanglement loss and latency, crucial factors in realizing the full potential of this technology. The theoretical framework presented here introduces a fundamentally new paradigm for network architecture, moving beyond classical constraints and towards a quantum-enhanced communication infrastructure. The primary focus is on the theoretical design and optimization of routing protocols specifically tailored for entangled quantum networks. We outline a methodology for simulating and optimizing quantum routing algorithms, acknowledging the challenges associated with decoherence and entanglement degradation. This work establishes a foundation for future research and development in quantum networking and routing.

title: Ashen Desert Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Nocturnal Bat
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Ashen Desert Bat" (ADB), inspired by the foraging strategies of bats inhabiting arid desert environments. These bats exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting scarce food resources. The ADB algorithm leverages key aspects of their behavior, including spatial memory, path following, and adaptive exploration-exploitation, to develop a robust optimization technique. The algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on a "memory map" reminiscent of the bat's echolocation system. The core components of ADB involve a dynamic adjustment of the memory map, a probabilistic path-following mechanism mimicking bat flight patterns, and an adaptive parameter control scheme that balances exploration and exploitation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The results indicate that ADB exhibits superior convergence speed and solution quality in several test cases. Further, the paper presents the mathematical formulation of the algorithm and its key parameters, providing a comprehensive understanding of its operational principles.

This research aims to provide a viable pathway for tackling computationally intensive dynamical systems simulations, offering a dramatic reduction in time and resource requirements.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Algorithms for Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to accelerate combinatorial optimization algorithms. Traditional combinatorial optimization problems, such as the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) and the Integer Linear Programming (ILP), often require exponential time to solve with classical algorithms. We propose a framework leveraging quantum algorithms, specifically the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), to tackle these problems. The core idea involves mapping the optimization problem into a quantum circuit, where the VQE algorithm iteratively refines a quantum state to find the optimal solution. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, focusing on the challenges and opportunities associated with quantum state preparation, measurement, and error mitigation. The paper provides a conceptual outline of the methodology and discusses potential improvements and future research directions. We demonstrate the feasibility of applying quantum computing to combinatorial optimization and highlight the potential for significant speedups compared to classical methods, especially as quantum hardware matures.

title: Dynamic Network Neuron Self-Organization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dynamic network neuron self-organization algorithm designed to adaptively adjust the connection strengths and topological structure of a neural network in response to environmental changes and evolving task demands. The core of the algorithm utilizes either reinforcement learning or evolutionary algorithms to optimize the network's parameters. Unlike traditional static self-organization methods, this approach enables continuous learning and adaptation, leading to improved performance in dynamic and complex environments. The algorithm's key components include a network topology generator, a connection weight optimizer, and a feedback mechanism for monitoring and adjusting the network's behavior. Simulation results demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in achieving robust and efficient network formation and adaptation compared to established methods. The potential applications span diverse fields, including robotics, artificial intelligence, and adaptive control systems.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum Entanglement as a Computational Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a uniquely quantum phenomenon, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. While its immediate implications for practical applications remain largely theoretical, recent advancements in quantum hardware and communication protocols have fueled renewed interest in exploring its use as a fundamental computational paradigm. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging non-local quantum entanglement to construct a computational framework capable of performing complex calculations across extended distances, offering a pathway to bypass the limitations of classical communication. This work explores the design of a protocol centered around creating a 'quantum bridge' between distant qubits, facilitating parallel processing of intricate computations. We argue that this approach, if successfully realized, could fundamentally alter the landscape of computational possibilities.

title: ## Arabian Sheath-tailed Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Sheath-tail Bat Optimization (SBO)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Arabian sheath-tailed bat ( *Tadarida thrasei*). This algorithm leverages the bat's unique hunting strategy – utilizing frequency-modulated ultrasonic calls – to efficiently explore the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. SBO incorporates a novel parameter, the "Echo Intensity," which dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance based on the bat's perceived information density. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, mimicking the bats' collective intelligence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SBO through its application to several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The core of SBO lies in the adaptive adjustment of the search radius and the 'Echo Intensity' parameter, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. The algorithm's design emphasizes robustness and adaptability, making it suitable for a broad range of complex optimization challenges. The performance evaluation is presented using metrics like convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational cost.

title: ## The Australian Magpie-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AMIOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Australian Magpie-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AMIOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of Australian Magpies. Magpies are known for their intelligent and adaptive search strategies when locating food sources. AMIOA leverages this behavior by mimicking the magpie's exploratory and exploitative phases, combined with a novel 'nest-building' mechanism to represent and refine solutions. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, similar to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), but incorporates a dynamic weighting system influenced by the perceived 'richness' of the search space, mirroring a magpie's tendency to prioritize promising areas. The core innovation lies in the 'nest' representation, which provides a compact and informative summary of the current solution, guiding the search towards more promising regions. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailing its key components and operational rules, and providing a conceptual framework for its implementation.

title: The Mantis-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mantis-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of the Chinese praying mantis. MIASA leverages the mantis's unique ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on prey movement and environmental changes. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameter adjustment, a multi-stage search process mimicking the mantis's stalking, attack, and retreat behavior, and a novel "focusing" mechanism designed to concentrate exploration around promising regions of the search space. The core of MIASA lies in its dynamically adjusted 'attack range' and 'observation interval', which are governed by an adaptive rule set derived from observed mantis behavior. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods in complex, non-convex optimization landscapes. Future research will focus on implementing MIASA in various benchmark problems and evaluating its performance through simulations.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Automated Hypothesis Generation in Scientific Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to scientific discovery leveraging probabilistic programming for automated hypothesis generation. The core idea is to represent complex scientific theories as probabilistic programs, allowing for exploration of parameter spaces and the generation of testable hypotheses. This work outlines the methodology, focusing on the integration of probabilistic modeling with the iterative process of hypothesis formation, testing, and refinement. The system dynamically adapts to data, prioritizing hypotheses with high probability and minimizing the need for human intervention in the initial stages of exploration. The potential impact of this approach on accelerating scientific research is significant, offering a framework for systematically investigating complex systems and identifying new research avenues. The paper details a framework for representing scientific theories using probabilistic programs, generating hypotheses based on parameter space exploration, and evaluating the consistency of generated hypotheses with observed data. It emphasizes the role of probabilistic inference in guiding the hypothesis generation process and provides a conceptual architecture for such a system. Furthermore, the paper highlights the advantages of this approach in terms of objectivity, efficiency, and the ability to uncover hidden relationships within data.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Counterfactual Exploration
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the process of reasoning about what would have happened if something had been different – is a cornerstone of human decision-making and a critical component of causal inference. However, traditional causal Bayesian networks often struggle to perform robust counterfactual reasoning, especially when dealing with unobserved latent variables that significantly influence the system under investigation. This paper introduces a novel framework for addressing this challenge, integrating latent counterfactual exploration using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. The core mechanism involves iteratively sampling counterfactual scenarios while explicitly modeling the influence of these latent variables through a latent space representation. This approach enhances the reliability of counterfactual inference by accounting for the potentially confounding effects of unobserved factors. The resulting model provides a statistically rigorous combination of causal inference and counterfactual reasoning, overcoming limitations of existing approaches and offering a more nuanced understanding of causal relationships. The proposed method's ability to handle latent variables is key to its robustness and applicability in diverse scenarios where causal relationships are complex and incompletely understood.

The system is designed to handle sequential data and infer complex relationships based on temporal dependencies, offering a pathway toward more intelligent and reliable AI systems. The key contribution lies in providing a formal framework for reasoning about the evolution of states, allowing for verifiable and consistent conclusions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unprecedented information security and, potentially, ultra-fast communication. This paper explores the development of a novel quantum entanglement information encoding and decoding algorithm, leveraging the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled states. We propose a new approach to secure communication and quantum computation, focusing on a dynamic encoding scheme that adapts to the environment, enhancing data resilience and offering potential for novel quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around establishing and managing entangled states, enabling secure key distribution and efficient data transfer. We investigate the potential of this algorithm in various quantum computing applications, including quantum key distribution and quantum state manipulation. This research delves into the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental investigations of this algorithm, highlighting its advantages and challenges.

title: Nonlinear Topological Quantum Computation: Adaptive Topology Encoding
abstract: This paper explores the potential of nonlinear topological quantum computation, focusing on the development of an adaptive topology encoding scheme. The core idea is to leverage quantum entanglement and the inherent adaptability of topological phases to dynamically adjust the structure of the encoded topology. This approach promises to enhance the efficiency of quantum computations by enabling real-time adjustments to the encoded quantum state. The work investigates the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and potential applications of this novel technique. We present a framework for generating and manipulating topological structures through entanglement, demonstrating its capability to create and adapt to varying quantum environments. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of this innovative approach on the field of quantum information science.

title: HYED-Net: unified hierarchical feature refinement for co-registered nuclei segmentation and virtual IHC-to-mpIF staining
abstract: Achieving precise nuclei delineation from routine immunohistochemistry (IHC) images remains challenging because of staining variability and densely touching cells. In this work, we propose HYED-Net, a unified framework that jointly synthesizes co-registered virtual staining channels and predicts nuclei segmentation. The generated staining channels are used as auxiliary features within a segmentation-oriented refinement pathway. The segmentation head combines an Evidence-weighted Dirichlet Gate (ED-Gate) for dual-branch feature fusion, SS2D spatial mixing at selected encoder and decoder stages, and HyperKernel Skip Injection (HKSI) for auxiliary-conditioned depthwise skip modulation. Across three random seeds, HYED-Net obtains a Dice coefficient of $$0.758\pm 0.005$$ and an AJI of $$0.588\pm 0.010$$ on BCData, and a Dice coefficient of $$0.764\pm 0.002$$ and an AJI of $$0.470\pm 0.001$$ on DeepLIIF. Together, these results demonstrate stable in-domain performance and support the feasibility of joint virtual staining and nuclei segmentation within a unified feature-refinement framework.

title: Every Nonrecursive Many-One Degree Contains Either One or Infinitely Many Finite-One Degrees
abstract: This paper proves that every nonrecursive many-one degree contains either exactly one or infinitely many finite-one degrees. This gives a negative answer to Open Question 2 of Richter, Stephan, and Zhang~\cite[p.~17]{RSZ}. Earlier work established that, for almost every AsubseteqN with respect to the standard product measure on 2^N, the degree [A]_{m} contains an infinite antichain of finite-one degrees~Cintioli. Thus the question had already received an almost-sure negative answer; the present theorem settles it for every nonrecursive many-one degree.

title: Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and Logarithmic Communication Cost
abstract: We study federated online reinforcement learning with linear function approximation. While recent multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms achieve strong regret guarantees, they typically require sharing raw trajectories. This reliance incurs a communication cost that scales linearly with the number of episodes and violates the privacy constraints of federated settings. To address these limitations, we propose Fed-LSVI, the first provably efficient federated algorithm for online reinforcement learning with linear function approximation in episodic Markov decision processes. By integrating a determinant-based event-triggered synchronization with a stepwise backward update mechanism, Fed-LSVI enables agents to collaboratively learn an optimal policy by exchanging only compressed sufficient statistics. We prove that Fed-LSVI achieves a regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sqrt{Md^3H^4T})$, where $d$ is the feature dimension, $H$ is the horizon length, $M$ is the number of agents, and $T$ is the number of episodes per agent, matching the best-known regret for multi-agent online reinforcement learning with linear function approximation. Moreover, by following the stringent communication and privacy constraints of the federated setting, Fed-LSVI reduces the communication cost to only logarithmic dependence on $T$, representing a significant improvement over prior methods.

title: Size-Independent Robustness in Multipartite Bell Self-Testing
abstract: Practical robust self-testing of multipartite entanglement has so far been restricted to small-scale systems due to error bounds that degrade severely with system size. In this work, we establish multipartite self-testing with robustness independent of the size of the quantum network. We derive a fully analytic, device-independent self-testing bound for $n$-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states. The bound scales linearly with the observed violation error and lies universally within a constant factor of two from a theoretical upper bound. Furthermore, the operator-inequality framework reduces the verification of the conjectured optimal bound to a highly efficient numerical check, which we perform up to $n=100$. Consequently, GHZ entanglement can be certified under a fixed noise level in arbitrarily large systems, enabling scalable device-independent verification.

title: Measuring Memory and Generalization as Separable Geometric Channels: The Topo^2 Framework
abstract: Deep networks trained on noisy labels simultaneously generalize on clean data and memorize flipped labels. These are usually conflated as pressures on one capacity. We present Topo^2, a measurement framework that makes them causally separable, measurable, and law-governed. Persistent-homology H1 structure of the representation space separates into a within-class manifold channel (a function of the training stopping point) and a cross-class channel (a monotone readout of memorized flipped samples). An intervention, the FM0 prescription (zero loss on flipped samples from epoch 0), reaches each setting's generalization ceiling while memorizing essentially nothing. Within the framework we establish a law set with graded evidence: (L2) FM0 separation prescription (9/9); (L1) the within-channel as a training-position function (mid-rise 6/6; convergence-back CIFAR 3/3, SVHN 2/3); (L3) a ring-construction identity (definitional, not a law); and TLS (memory-generalization topological layering): memory is causally additive, anchored (silencing clean collapses the representation), invertible (stripping memory restores near-ceiling generalization), and quantitatively billable (the memorization cost law, effective slope coefficient C ~ 0.38 at the reference capacity: CIFAR-10 0.3801 / SVHN 0.3806 / CIFAR-100 0.384 / VGG 0.3715, capacity-dependent in general and traced to clean-sample feature displacement). We also publish the framework's boundaries: a falsification ledger of nine dead ends, and an instrument-vindication section that excludes six families of global statistics as explanations of the within-channel. The framework turns "memorization" from an ill-defined capacity into a measurable, separable, invertible topological layer.

title: Sublinear Space Graph Algorithms in the Continual Release Model
abstract: The graph continual release model of differential privacy seeks to produce differentially private solutions to graph problems under a stream of edge updates where new private solutions are released after each update. Previously known edge differentially private algorithms for most graph problems including densest subgraph and matchings in the continual release setting only output real-valued estimates (not vertex subset solutions) and do not use sublinear space. In this paper, we leverage sparsification to address the above shortcomings for edge-insertion streams. Our edge differentially private algorithms use sublinear space with respect to the number of edges in the graph. In addition, for the densest subgraph problem, we output edge differentially private vertex subset solutions; no previous graph algorithms in the continual release model output such subsets. We make novel use of sparsification techniques from the non-private streaming and static graph algorithms literature to achieve new results in the sublinear space continual release setting. This includes algorithms for densest subgraph, maximum matching, and the first continual release k-core decomposition algorithm. To complement our insertion-only algorithms, we conclude with polynomial additive error lower bounds for edge-privacy in the fully dynamic setting, where only logarithmic lower bounds were previously known.

title: Comparative Performance Analysis of SVM, LSTM, and IndoBERT for Sentiment Analysis of User Reviews
abstract: The Maganghub Kemnaker National Internship Program, launched on October 1, 2025, attracted significant public attention while also generating both criticism and praise on the social media platform X. This study compares the performance of three classification algorithms—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and IndoBERT—for sentiment analysis of public opinions regarding the program. The dataset consists of 6,825 Indonesian-language tweets collected between October and December 2025 after duplicate removal. The data were preprocessed and labeled as positive, neutral, or negative using two approaches: automated labeling with a Hugging Face model and manual annotation. Each algorithm was evaluated under five hyperparameter tuning scenarios using an 80:20 train–test split and assessed with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results show that IndoBERT achieved the highest performance, with an accuracy of 85.27% using the Hugging Face–labeled dataset, outperforming SVM (79.05%) and LSTM (78.68%). IndoBERT's superior performance is attributed to its Transformer-based architecture and multi-head self-attention mechanism, which effectively capture bidirectional contextual information, including sarcastic expressions commonly found in social media posts. The findings were further implemented in a web-based dashboard to support interactive public opinion monitoring for policymakers.

title: A Combination of Forward Chaining and Certainty Factor Methods in a Child Mental Health Expert System with Accuracy Comparison Using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire
abstract: The increasing complexity of child mental health issues requires accurate detection and intelligent decision-support systems for early identification and intervention. This study analyses emotional and behavioural difficulties among 500 children aged 11–17 years using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) dataset and develops an expert system integrating Forward Chaining and Certainty Factor methods. Results indicate that most respondents had relatively low difficulty levels across SDQ dimensions, although substantial proportions showed high Emotional Symptoms and Conduct Problems scores, suggesting potential psychological concerns. The proposed expert system achieved 90% accuracy, demonstrating good performance in distinguishing Normal and Abnormal categories, although classification of the Borderline category remained challenging. Higher scores in Emotional Symptoms, Conduct Problems, Hyperactivity, and Peer Problems, alongside lower Prosocial Behaviour scores, were associated with greater likelihood of Borderline or Abnormal classification. These findings demonstrate that integrating Forward Chaining and Certainty Factor can effectively support early screening and decision-making in child mental health assessment.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Fraud Investigations: A Critical Review.
abstract: Abstract: AI significantly influences the financial fraud investigations across different parts of the workflow related to detection, automation, transactions prioritization, anomalous discovery, and fraud investigation explanations. This approach has documented highest performance metrics across empirical studies, to support detecting fraud in a set number of parameters. Random assessment gave up to 96% Accuracy (with a 98.9% Area under the curve); fuzzy logistic regression provides an AUC up to >0.99, with up to 0.90+ Sensitivity and Specificity on credit-card. Fraud investigation explanation AI ensemble “FraudX AI” provides 95% Recall and a 97% AUCPRC” (Afriyie et al., 2023; Baisholan et al., 2025; Charizanos et al., 2024). Machine learning cut unexpected losses by 15% compared with static heuristics. Meanwhile economic optimization showed a further reduction in expected losses and produced false positive rate of 0.4 percent (Vanini et al., 2023) which shows, that machine intelligence actually carries some operational weight once it predicts results in a financial decision. Although some performance measures that are heterogeneous among studies such as - a variety of approaches does not include specificity (often called precision), sensitivity (sometimes referred to as recall, or true positive rate), expected lost value added (often denoted by false positive burden, that for financial decision tasks refers to economic value) is frequently missed from reporting. None of the surveyed machine learning applications has achieved reasonable industrial applicability from their authors own perspective, except that there are few surveyed approaches which for an assessment of scalability and reliability are reported with reasonable degree of success in an industrial environment. (Ryman-Tubb et al., 2018). Explainability appears to be the furthest behind in Anti money laundering (AML) applications with 51% of machine learning models under review being categorized noninterpretable and no documented application of explainable AI reported at the time of writing in AML literature (Kute et al. 2021). On the whole AI best functions as a support in an investigation, not a tool that replaces auditor, compliance officer or investigation. Its effectiveness is related to managing class imbalance, dealing with dynamic fraud profiles, using privacy-preserving methods for data sharing, accurate labelling and obtaining evidence that can be understood by humans and is verifiable institution-to-institution, jurisdiction-to-jurisdiction.

title: 基于自适应的神经元网络的强化学习算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm based on adaptive neuron networks, designed to automate the learning and parameter adjustment of neural network structures. The core innovation lies in a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism driven by environment feedback, coupled with an adaptive learning process that optimizes the network's topology. The algorithm aims to improve the efficiency of reinforcement learning by reducing the reliance on manual tuning and promoting more robust and adaptable neural network configurations. We analyze the algorithm's performance across diverse tasks and demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving significant improvements in training speed and generalization ability compared to traditional RL methods.

title: Adaptive Compression Techniques for Streaming Data
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional compression algorithms when applied to streaming data, which inherently exhibits dynamic and variable statistical properties. The core idea presented is a novel adaptive compression technique that leverages machine learning to dynamically adjust its compression parameters in real-time. title: Self-Supervised Learning for Discovering Graph Embeddings
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have achieved significant success in various graph-related tasks, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. However, a critical limitation of many GNN approaches is their dependence on large amounts of labeled data for training. Obtaining such labeled data can be costly, time-consuming, and often impractical, particularly for large and complex graphs. This paper proposes a novel approach to learning graph embeddings using self-supervised learning (SSL). We hypothesize that intrinsic relationships within a graph structure can be leveraged to learn informative embeddings without relying on explicit labels. Our method utilizes self-supervised tasks designed to exploit the graph's connectivity and structure. Specifically, we explore techniques like contrastive learning and masked node prediction to learn embeddings that capture the underlying graph topology. We demonstrate that our self-supervised approach can learn effective graph embeddings, achieving comparable or superior performance compared to traditional supervised methods when labeled data is scarce. The key contributions of this work are the application of SSL to graph embedding learning and the design of novel self-supervised tasks tailored for graph data.

The presented approach aims to address limitations of traditional machine learning algorithms by incorporating quantum computational principles. This research investigates the potential benefits of such a hybrid approach, presenting a framework for leveraging quantum topology to accelerate and refine machine learning models.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization via Wave Function Mirroring
abstract: Quantum information processing demands robust synchronization across distributed quantum systems. Current approaches often struggle with maintaining coherence over significant distances, limiting the scalability of quantum computations. This paper introduces a novel protocol, Wave Function Mirroring, designed to address this challenge by utilizing wave function mirroring to synchronize quantum states across multiple locations. The algorithm meticulously mirrors the evolution of quantum states, mitigating decoherence effects and facilitating distributed quantum computations with enhanced coherence. We present a rigorous mathematical framework and detailed implementation demonstrating the protocol's effectiveness in achieving synchronized states.

title: QUED V2 — Vom unproduktiven KI-Fehler zur viable Alternative
abstract: Abstract QUED V2 formalisiert die Mechanik, durch die KI Fehler von unproduktiven Abweichungen zu strukturierten, kognitiv verwertbaren Alternativen werden. Der Artikel zeigt, dass die Produktivität eines Fehlers durch zwei Faktoren bestimmt wird: die Komplexität des semantischen Raums und die Fidelity des kognitiven Transfers. Hohe Komplexität kombiniert mit hoher Fidelity erzeugt Fehler, die keine Fehlleistungen darstellen, sondern viable alternative Interpretationen. Durch wiederholte, ausgerichtete Divergenz stabilisiert QUED Bedeutungsräume, minimiert Drift, erhöht Auditierbarkeit und macht Sicherheit emergent. QUED V2 bildet damit die mechanische Grundlage für die in QUED V3 dargestellte angewandte kognitive Architektur.

title: Title: Geometric Modeling of Cognitive Processes
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing geometric modeling to represent and analyze cognitive processes. The fundamental premise is that cognitive states, traditionally understood through complex neural networks, can be elegantly captured through geometric abstractions. We propose a framework wherein cognitive states are visualized as geometric objects – points, lines, surfaces, and more complex shapes – enabling deeper insights into brain function through visualization and analysis. This approach moves beyond traditional symbolic representations, offering a potentially more intuitive and readily interpretable model. We aim to demonstrate the utility of this framework for exploring and understanding various cognitive phenomena. The core mechanism involves translating abstract cognitive states into geometric forms, facilitating the identification of patterns and relationships that might be obscured by more complex neural network representations.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing quantum error correction (QEC) codes, termed Dynamic QEC Code Optimization (DQCO). The core claim is to dynamically adjust both the encoding and decoding parameters of QEC codes to enhance their error correction performance. The proposed mechanism involves real-time adaptation of the encoding rate and decoding strategy based on the observed communication environment and noise levels. This approach strengthens the adaptive capacity of QEC codes, allowing them to better meet the demands of complex communication scenarios. The algorithm employs a feedback loop, continuously monitoring the channel characteristics and adjusting the QEC parameters accordingly. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the optimization process, including the channel capacity estimation, the rate distortion function analysis, and the adaptive adjustment of the coding and decoding parameters. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in error correction performance compared to static QEC schemes.

title: Quantum-Inspired Simulated Annealing for Global Optimization
abstract: Simulated annealing (SA) is a widely used metaheuristic algorithm for global optimization, particularly effective in tackling complex, high-dimensional search spaces. However, SA's performance is often hampered by its susceptibility to getting trapped within local minima, significantly restricting its ability to discover the true global optimum. This paper proposes a novel quantum-inspired modification of the standard SA algorithm, termed Quantum-Inspired Simulated Annealing (QISA). QISA incorporates principles from quantum mechanics, specifically quantum tunneling and superposition, to augment SA's exploration capabilities. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the temperature schedule based on probabilistic quantum effects, enabling the algorithm to more effectively navigate the solution landscape and escape local minima. The proposed approach is evaluated theoretically and through a detailed mathematical analysis, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the convergence rate and solution quality for various global optimization problems. The algorithm's core mechanism relies on transitioning between states with a probability dictated by a quantum-inspired acceptance criterion, rather than solely relying on a fixed temperature schedule. This introduces an element of stochasticity and allows for more directed exploration of the search space. The evaluation results showcase a notable improvement over traditional SA in several benchmark problems.

title: Causal Graph Learning with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal graph learning leveraging the strengths of reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional methods for discovering causal relationships often falter when confronted with high-dimensional datasets and intricate feedback loops, frequently relying on assumptions that may not hold true in real-world scenarios. Our framework addresses these limitations by training an RL agent to iteratively construct a causal graph. The agent's actions involve modifying the graph – adding or removing edges – based on observed system behavior. The reward signal is determined by the accuracy of predictions made using the current graph representation. This integration of causal inference with RL enables the network to adapt and learn causal relationships within complex, dynamic environments, offering a potentially more robust and scalable solution compared to conventional techniques. We outline the core principles, the proposed agent architecture, and the reward function design.

title: Biafran Palm Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Paraxanthoryctes krauzanni*
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, Biafran Palm Squirrel (BPS), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Paraxanthoryctes krauzanni*, a squirrel species endemic to the Biafra region. The algorithm mimics the squirrel's efficient search strategy for food resources, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation. BPS utilizes a novel adaptive population management scheme, a modified Lévy flight mechanism, and a dynamic weight adjustment strategy based on the relative fitness of individuals. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BPS is robust and adaptable, offering a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm revolves around maintaining a diverse population while strategically directing search efforts towards promising regions of the search space. We demonstrate its effectiveness through numerical simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential advantages in various applications.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Key Agreement Protocol
abstract: This paper presents a novel key agreement protocol leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The protocol, termed the "Quantum Entanglement Key Agreement Protocol" (QEKAP), aims to establish a shared secret key between two parties, Alice and Bob, without relying on classical communication channels for key exchange. The core of the protocol utilizes entangled photon pairs to generate correlated random keys, followed by the application of quantum error correction codes to mitigate the effects of noise and ensure accurate key transmission. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and highlight its potential advantages over traditional key exchange methods, specifically addressing vulnerabilities associated with eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks. The protocol's security rests on the fundamental laws of quantum mechanics, namely the no-cloning theorem and the uncertainty principle. The key parameters influencing the protocol's performance, such as entanglement fidelity and the overhead introduced by the quantum error correction scheme, are analyzed. Simulation results indicate that QEKAP provides a robust and secure solution for key distribution in quantum networks.

title: The Quantum Algorithmic Optimization of Self-Organized Structures
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-organized quantum algorithms to optimize complex geometric structures. Traditional quantum algorithms are often limited by the inherent challenges of quantum systems, particularly in maintaining coherence and entanglement. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages the dynamic nature of graphs to guide the optimization process, enabling global optimization of complex geometries. The core mechanism centers around the design of a self-organizing quantum algorithm that adapts to the structure of the problem, iteratively refining the solution towards the desired outcome. The research explores the potential of using graph representations to model the geometric structure, and the resulting algorithm's ability to enhance the performance of various optimization tasks. The paper introduces a framework for evaluating the effectiveness of such algorithms using a defined metric. Finally, the work discusses the theoretical implications and potential future directions of this approach.

title: 基于拓扑的机器学习模型优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning model optimization based on topological structure. The core idea is to leverage the inherent topology of the model's parameters to enhance both model performance and generalization ability. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the model's structure to promote robustness and reduce overfitting. This approach contrasts with traditional optimization techniques which often rely on local adjustments. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through a series of experiments comparing it to established optimization strategies. The results indicate significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness, particularly in complex datasets.

title: ## The Nautilus-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NASAL)
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (NASAL), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and shell morphology of the Nautilus shell. The algorithm leverages the Nautilus's ability to maintain a stable position while adapting its path to navigate complex environments, mirroring a strategy of exploring diverse solutions while retaining promising ones. NASAL incorporates elements of both adaptive step size control, mimicking the Nautilus's subtle movements, and a dynamic neighborhood structure, reflecting the shell's layered design. The core of NASAL lies in a novel 'Spiral-Adaptive Exploration' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance, and a 'Shell-Based Cluster' strategy for solution representation and diversification. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, detailed implementation, and discusses its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Complex Systems Simulation
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference (QEBI) presents a novel approach to complex systems simulation, aiming to significantly improve model accuracy through the application of quantum mechanics in Bayesian inference. This paper introduces a new algorithm, the 'Quantum-Guided Bayesian Network' (QGBN), designed to overcome the computational limitations inherent in traditional Bayesian methods when dealing with highly complex systems. QEBI leverages quantum mechanics to enhance probabilistic inference, reducing computational cost while maintaining high accuracy. The QGBN employs a quantum-guided process that minimizes the influence of noise and allows for more precise uncertainty quantification. We demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations of a dynamic, multi-layered system exhibiting complex interactions and sensitivity to initial conditions. The results show substantial improvements in model accuracy and reduced computational time compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Sensing Based on Quantum Noise
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum sensing that fundamentally shifts the perspective on quantum noise. Instead of viewing it as an unwanted disturbance, we argue that quantum noise is a critical resource for extracting subtle environmental information. The core concept involves designing a quantum sensor that leverages the statistical properties of quantum noise to precisely measure and interpret its distribution, ultimately enabling the detection of extremely weak signals. This approach moves beyond traditional quantum sensing methodologies which often rely on minimizing noise. We present a theoretical framework and mathematical formalism for this concept, outlining the principles of operation and potential performance characteristics. The underlying mechanism hinges on the ability to correlate the statistical fluctuations of quantum noise with the underlying environmental signal. This work represents a significant departure from conventional thinking and offers a new paradigm for quantum sensing technology. ---

title: Ansell's Epauletted Fruit Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Ansell's Epauletted Fruit Bat Algorithm" (AEFBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Ansellus noctivagus*, the epauletted fruit bat. These bats exhibit a complex and efficient foraging strategy characterized by a unique 'epauletting' behavior – strategically positioning themselves to maximize their access to food sources. We model this behavior as a multi-dimensional optimization problem and translate it into a new algorithm that combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). AEFBA utilizes a dynamic 'epaulet' assignment mechanism, where each particle (representing a potential solution) dynamically adjusts its position based on the relative food availability (fitness) of neighboring particles. The algorithm incorporates a 'social influence' factor, mimicking the bats' tendency to follow the most successful foragers. The performance of AEFBA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The algorithm's key features, including the dynamic epaulet assignment and social influence, are detailed, and its convergence characteristics are analyzed. Results indicate that AEFBA provides a competitive solution to several challenging optimization problems, demonstrating the potential of biomimicry in algorithm design.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Deep Learning Representation Learning
abstract: This work investigates the potential information-theoretic limits of deep learning representation learning. It proposes a framework utilizing concepts from information theory – entropy, mutual information, and Kolmogorov complexity – to quantitatively assess information loss throughout the deep learning process, from initial feature extraction to final representation learning. The core argument is that current deep learning architectures may be approaching fundamental limitations as dictated by information theory, specifically concerning the irreducible complexity of data. The research identifies critical thresholds where excessive information loss compromises model performance, suggesting avenues for designing more efficient and robust architectures or altering training strategies to minimize this loss. This approach offers a rigorous, information-theoretic foundation for evaluating deep learning models and potentially guiding future research directions.

title: Angolan Long-Eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bat Echo Algorithm" (BEA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Angolan long-eared bat (Plecotus Tanzaniensis). These bats utilize a unique echolocation strategy, adjusting their flight paths based on the reflected echoes to efficiently locate food sources in complex environments. The BEA leverages this adaptation process by employing a population of 'bats' exploring a search space. Each bat's movement is governed by a dynamic adjustment of its echo intensity, proportional to the reflected signal strength. The algorithm incorporates parameters mimicking the bat's behaviour, such as an echo intensity, a frequency, and a flight angle, to guide the search process. Specifically, the algorithm uses the following key equations: * Position Update: $x_{i+1}^k = x_i^k + \alpha_k \Delta x_i^k$, where $x_i^k$ is the position of the *i*-th bat at iteration *k*, $\alpha_k$ is the learning factor, and $\Delta x_i^k$ is the step size determined by the echo intensity. * Echo Intensity Update: $I_{i+1}^k = I_i^k + \beta_k (I_i^k - I_{best}^k)$, where $I_i^k$ is the echo intensity of the *i*-th bat at iteration *k*, $I_{best}^k$ is the maximum echo intensity found so far, and $\beta_k$ is the echo adjustment factor. * Frequency Adjustment: $f_{i+1}^k = f_i^k + \gamma_k (f_i^k - f_{avg}^k)$, where $f_i^k$ is the frequency of the *i*-th bat at iteration *k*, $f_{avg}^k$ is the average frequency of the population, and $\gamma_k$ is the frequency adjustment factor. * Fitness Evaluation: $Fitness(x_i^k) = -\sum_{j=1}^{N} |x_i^k - x^*_j|$, where $x_i^k$ is the position of the *i*-th bat, $x^*_j$ represents the best solution found so far, and *N* is the number of solutions. The BEA exhibits promising performance in solving a range of complex optimization problems, including continuous optimization, combinatorial optimization, and function optimization. The algorithm's parameters are tuned to optimize its convergence rate and solution quality. The results demonstrate the BEA's effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization.

title: Explainable AI for Deep Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models have demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks, but their inherent complexity often leads to a lack of interpretability. These models are frequently referred to as "black boxes," making it challenging to understand the rationale behind their decisions. This paper proposes a novel approach to explain DRL models by leveraging counterfactual reasoning. We introduce a framework that generates counterfactual examples – "what if" scenarios – by systematically altering the input state and observing the resulting changes in the agent's actions. These counterfactual examples reveal the critical factors driving the agent's behavior, offering a more transparent and understandable explanation of the DRL model's decision-making process. The core of our method relies on identifying the minimal changes in the input that lead to a change in the agent's policy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications in various DRL domains. Our approach offers a pathway towards building more trustworthy and reliable DRL systems.

title: ## Blackspot Rhineland Codon Polarized Adaptive Search (BRCPAS) Algorithm
abstract: The blackspot rhineland codon ( *Lophiomusmus manetti*) exhibits remarkable adaptability to changing environmental conditions, particularly in its ability to dynamically adjust its bioluminescence patterns – a process often referred to as "codon polarization". This paper introduces the Blackspot Rhineland Codon Polarized Adaptive Search (BRCPAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by this unique biological behavior. BRCPAS utilizes a polarization mechanism, analogous to the codon's light modulation, to selectively explore and exploit the search space. The algorithm maintains a population of potential solutions, each associated with a 'polarization vector' representing its dominance in a given region. The polarization vectors are iteratively adjusted based on the objective function value and the diversity of the population, promoting both convergence and exploration. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its adaptive nature and suitability for complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum Adaptive Algorithm-Based Graph Neural Network (QAGAN)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Quantum Adaptive Algorithms (QAA) to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). We propose a novel QAGAN architecture that leverages quantum self-optimization to enhance the training and inference process of GNNs. The core of this approach is a dynamically adjusted parameter set derived from quantum self-adaptation, allowing the network to effectively handle complex graph structures. We explore the benefits of this method, focusing on improved performance and robustness compared to traditional GNN algorithms. The proposed QAGAN offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and scalable GNN applications across diverse domains.

title: Quantum State-Based Distributed Time Travel Algorithm (QSTTA)
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of a distributed time travel algorithm leveraging quantum state manipulation. The core concept revolves around simulating quantum time travel through precise control of quantum states, utilizing quantum entanglement and quantum gates. We propose a novel approach to time travel that transcends conventional theoretical models, offering potential for accurate temporal manipulation. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implications of this algorithm, focusing on the core mechanism of state transformation and the role of quantum entanglement. The goal is to present a mathematically rigorous framework for time travel simulation, addressing key challenges related to accuracy and control. The potential impact of this algorithm extends beyond theoretical exploration, suggesting a paradigm shift in our understanding of time and its manipulation.

title: ## American Lion: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the American Lion
abstract: This paper presents American Lion, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of the American lion (Panthera leo atrox). The algorithm leverages the lion's strategic movement, hunting tactics, and social dynamics to create a robust and efficient search process. American Lion incorporates key features such as a dynamic territory exploration, a sophisticated decision-making mechanism based on relative fitness, and a social interaction component simulating the lion's collaborative hunting. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The core mechanics are defined by the following: a territory representation, a movement strategy based on fitness gradient, a decision-making rule for territory selection, and a social interaction mechanism for collaborative exploration. The performance of American Lion is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving global optimization. The algorithm is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to showcase its advantages in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The results demonstrate that American Lion provides a competitive and promising approach to tackling complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Complex Geometry Turing Machine
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize the design and analysis of complex geometric Turing machines. Traditional Turing machines rely heavily on explicit algorithm design, while the inherent properties of quantum entanglement offer a fundamentally different approach to simulating complex geometric patterns and behaviors. We propose a novel architecture leveraging entanglement to model geometric intuition more accurately, ultimately enabling the precise characterization of geometric Turing machine behavior. The core mechanism centers around encoding geometric information within entangled states, allowing for dynamic and nuanced geometric simulations. This work introduces a new framework for geometric Turing machine design, demonstrating the potential for significantly enhanced computational power and a deeper understanding of geometric computation.

title: 基于多模态数据融合的异常检测算法
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection leveraging the fusion of multi-modal data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on single data modalities, which can be susceptible to noise and limited in their ability to capture complex patterns indicative of anomalies. This research posits that integrating information from multiple sources – such as text, images, and audio – provides a more robust and accurate representation of the underlying system. The core mechanism involves a fusion technique that combines these disparate data streams, followed by an anomaly detection algorithm applied to the fused data. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance compared to single-modal approaches, particularly in scenarios with noisy or incomplete data. We present a framework for multi-modal fusion and anomaly detection, focusing on algorithmic design and performance evaluation. The proposed method aims to enhance the accuracy and robustness of anomaly detection systems across various applications.

title: ## Afroalpine Vlei Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Collective Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Vlei Rat Algorithm" (VRA), inspired by the collective foraging behavior of the Afroalpine Vlei Rat ( *Acomys subsp. vlei* ). These rats exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting sparse food resources in challenging environments. The VRA leverages this observed behavior, specifically the dynamic adjustments in search strategies and the emphasis on local exploitation, to create a robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a novel adaptive population management technique, termed "Patch Switching," and a refined exploitation phase based on a weighted sum of local search distances. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the VRA through simulations on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Powell's test functions. Results show that the VRA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of collective foraging strategies to design a metaheuristic algorithm and the demonstration of its superior performance across diverse optimization landscapes.

title: African Manatee Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Manatee Search Algorithm" (MSA), inspired by the foraging behavior of African manatees. Manatees exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources, characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation. The MSA leverages these behaviors to generate a new optimization algorithm designed for tackling complex, non-linear optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of manatee foraging, including a "scanning" mechanism for exploring the search space and a "focusing" mechanism for refining promising solutions. Mathematical formulations are presented to explain the core operations of the MSA, including the position update rule, the guiding vector generation, and the selection mechanism. The performance of the MSA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results show that MSA offers a competitive approach to optimization, particularly in scenarios where exploration and exploitation need to be carefully balanced. The algorithm's adaptive nature, stemming from the manatee's natural intelligence, allows it to navigate complex landscapes and converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions effectively.

Manatees exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources, characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation. The MSA leverages these behaviors to generate a new optimization algorithm designed for tackling complex, non-linear optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of manatee foraging, including a "scanning" mechanism for exploring the search space and a "focusing" mechanism for refining promising solutions. Mathematical formulations are presented to explain the core operations of the MSA, including the position update rule, the guiding vector generation, and the selection mechanism. The performance of the MSA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results show that MSA offers a competitive approach to optimization, particularly in scenarios where exploration and exploitation need to be carefully balanced. The algorithm's adaptive nature, stemming from the manatee's natural intelligence, allows it to navigate complex landscapes and converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions effectively.

title: 基于动态拓扑结构的量子计算验证
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for revolutionary computational capabilities, but its practical realization faces significant challenges, particularly in algorithm validation. Traditional verification methods often rely on classical algorithms and proofs, which struggle to capture the inherent complexities of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm verification technique based on dynamic topology, leveraging self-adaptive learning to dynamically adjust the quantum system's topology to ensure correctness and stability. We propose a mechanism that utilizes a continuous evolution of the system's geometry, allowing for a more precise and flexible validation process. This approach directly addresses the limitations of current methods, offering a promising pathway towards robust quantum algorithms. The paper details the theoretical framework, implementation of the self-adaptive learning algorithm, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of the proposed technique.
